[2026-08-15 EDT] — AWS cost reduction: Tier 1 executed, $676 tranche analysed, two premises withdrawn

Commit f284df44. Infrastructure only, no application code. ~$122.74/mo realised, against a list that estimated ~$580.

  • Paused 4 App Runner services — content-builder-dev, presentation-creator-dev, video-creator (mgmt) and velvet-groove (Staging-B). App Runner bills provisioned memory for all 730 h/month regardless of traffic; these served 182–1,324 requests over 30 days at an average of 0.002–0.009 active instances. velvet-groove alone is 12 GB / $61.32 mo, untagged, no stack, image never updated since 2026-07-05, zero requests in 30 days.
  • Deleted 4 stale CloudWatch dashboards (~$9.30/mo) — JSON bodies backed up to docs/aws-audit/2026-08-14/backups/ first, so restore is a put-dashboard away. Deleted 3 schoolonline* RDS snapshots from May 2022 after confirming both source DBs return DBInstanceNotFound.
  • 30-day retention on all 87 log groups that had none (71 mgmt + 16 staging-b). Zero compliance/audit groups affected. Worth ~$0.02/mo — done for hygiene, and the entry is explicit that it is not a cost measure.
  • ⚠️ Withdrew a recommendation made earlier the same session. voice-agent-api-waf-dev is not unattached and was not deleted. wafv2 list-resources-for-web-acl silently defaults to APPLICATION_LOAD_BALANCER; passing every --resource-type shows it protecting the live voice-agent-api-dev API Gateway stage (450 req/7d). Not removed (CDK-managed; Semi Prod will want pooling). voice-agent-nat-dev shows 0 bytes/7d but fronts 48 live VoiceDesk Lambdas — left alone. Billed VPC endpoints are Secrets Manager + SSM that in-VPC Lambdas depend on. The ElastiCache orphan (−$93/mo) was removed by another terminal at 20:33 via CFN (84e7545c), not by this session.
  • Blocked on Bill: AWS Business Support $232.00/mo — no downgrade API exists, and the SKU (AWS Business Support+, flat $29 × 8 accounts rather than greater-of-$100-or-10%) suggests a reseller-led plan that the console may refuse to cancel. Zero ChangeResourceRecordSets events that day confirm it was not caused by this work. video-creator.inspiresgenius.com is a real hostname and is down while paused.

[2026-08-14 EDT] — Surveys: new survey-service (build / take / results) + org exposure, AI parse, identity & enable toggle

A full Survey feature, built end to end this session and live on dev + staging-b: author surveys, expose them to an organization, collect responses centrally, and read a compilation — plus AI-assisted upload-to-build, a per-survey enable toggle, and creator/responder identity capture.

  • New microservice services/survey-service/ (FastAPI + Mangum Lambda, mirrors growth-service). Schema-isolated survey Postgres schema via RDS Proxy; surveys + survey_responses (JSONB) + Alembic baseline. Endpoints under /v1/surveys: list (?scope=take|manage), CRUD, submit response, individual responses, summary/compilation, and POST /parse.
  • Org exposure — surveys.org_id; a user's take-list is filtered to surveys exposed to their resolved org (no-org callers see NULL-org surveys, so zero-org environments aren't silently empty). Surfaced to the user role in Settings → My Workspace.
  • AI-assisted upload-to-build — upload/paste questions + answers + freeform text → a structured draft. Anthropic SDK direct (no Bedrock), key resolved at runtime from the shared secret, fail-open to a deterministic heuristic that handles checkbox options and 1–5 Likert rows.
  • Per-survey enable on/off toggle (surveys.enabled) — respondents only see enabled surveys; new surveys default OFF, existing stay ON. Builder switch + inline toggle in the manage list.
  • Creator + responder identity — name + email captured server-side from the verified identity (never client-supplied), shown in the manage list and per-response in Results.
  • Two bugs caught by verifying, not assuming: the API Gateway {proxy+} route did not match the bare /v1/surveys collection path (list/create 404'd); and strict org scoping made the take-list silently empty on zero-org staging-b. Both fixed and re-verified.
  • Deployed + verified on dev and staging-b (routes auth-gated, migrations applied, served bundles checked). Seeded a real Baseline Survey (22 questions, correctly typed) directly into both environments. Coordinated additively with a second terminal refining the same feature's authoring role model.

[2026-08-14 EDT] — Employer & sector question packs wired into the practice interview

The 138 curated questions from Employer_Interview_Question_Packs.docx now drive the candidate Interview Practice surface — Phases 1–3 of that document's build plan. Built and tested, NOT deployed.

  • New package app/employers/ — models.py, dataset.py (16 employer packs), sectors.py (7 sector packs), resolver.py. Plus GET /v1/agents/interview/employer-packs (catalogue, metadata only) and two optional fields — company, industry — on the tailored practice route.
  • Curated-first, model-second. A resolved pack's questions replace the sampled ones deterministically and are excluded from the LLM rewrite payload entirely; the model only contextualizes the competencies the pack does not cover, and gets the employer name as tone context with an explicit instruction not to imply these are that employer's real questions. A model that has never seen a company's question list must not be the thing asserting what is on it.
  • Resolver precision is a correctness issue. Whole-token matching after corporate-suffix stripping: “Blackstone” does not resolve to BlackRock, “Metagenics” does not resolve to Meta, “Citizens Bank” does not resolve to Citi. Each near-miss is pinned by test.
  • Fail-open everywhere. Unknown company, unknown industry, junk input, or a dead LLM all return a full 12-competency candidate-safe set; employer: null reproduces the previous behaviour exactly. Candidate-safety unchanged — no rubric, no 5/3/1 exemplars.
  • Parity is enforced, not assumed: scripts/check_employer_dataset_parity.py fails if the reviewed Word document and the runtime dataset drift, so the question that passed review is the question a candidate is asked. Verified with a negative control.
  • Verified: 5121 passed / 11 skipped across the full agent-engine suite; 111 new tests in tests/test_employer_packs.py.

  • Added docs/plans/Employer_Interview_Question_Packs.docx (18pp) via scripts/build_employer_interview_packs.py. Employers: Amazon/AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Oracle, LinkedIn, McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Deloitte, Accenture, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Bridgewater, BlackRock. Sectors: technology, consulting, financial services, healthcare/life sciences, aerospace & defence, retail/CPG, public sector & workforce. Question content lives in the script as data, so the packs are diffable in git rather than locked in a binary.
  • All 138 questions map to a real competency id in star_interview_bank.py — verified programmatically against the module, not by eye: 12/12 competencies used, zero unknown ids. The packs change what a question sounds like, never what is assessed — so no new rubric, scorer or evaluator change is implied.
  • Provenance discipline, mirroring app/role_pages: every pack names the employer’s OWN publicly published values or hiring framework. Questions are written by us in the style of that framework — explicitly not any company’s actual, internal or leaked questions, and no implication of endorsement or affiliation. The document leads with that statement.
  • ⚠️ Load-bearing discovery: InterviewFrame already carries company and industry — collected since the v2 frame, shown in the header, folded into Alex’s coaching context — but never passed to tailoring. getTailoredPracticeQuestions() takes no company and InterviewPracticePage.tsx branches on roleTitle alone. So the build is an extension of a live path: two optional request fields, one curated dataset, one resolver. No new service, store, bus or scoring model.
  • Curated-first, model-second is the design rule — a resolved employer question replaces the sampled base question deterministically, leaving the LLM only to contextualise to a role title. A model that has never seen a company’s question list must not be the thing asserting what is on it. Fail-open preserved: unknown company returns today’s behaviour with employer: null.

[2026-08-07] — Agent-engine: 180-test backlog cleared, CI gates armed for real

The suite was 180 failed / 4527 passed on development, invisible because both CI gates were no-ops: backend-ci.yml appended || true to pytest and pr-validation.yml checked three files. Now 4810 passed in CI with both enforcing. PRs #825 + #838, promoted to staging-b.

  • 117 of 180 were one fixture. ProviderFactory._providers is CLASS state registered once at import; any test calling reset() without restoring it left the registry empty for everything after, so later agents returned the “having trouble processing your request” apology at confidence 0.3. An autouse fixture re-registers per test.
  • Production bug — keyword classifier blind to punctuation. lower.split() meant “growth,” matched nothing while “help” matched BUSINESS, misrouting coaching messages. Now word-boundary tokenised; client/clients added to the business set.
  • Production bug — unbounded auth DB query. _resolve_canonical_sub ran inside require_auth on every authenticated request with no time limit; a wedged connection hangs the request. Now asyncio.wait_for-bounded.
  • Production bug — WS disconnect raised. Low-level receive() RETURNS websocket.disconnect rather than raising; nothing checked, so the loop came round and raised. Every disconnect exited via the error handler.
  • The hang: three stacked causes. pytest-asyncio ^0.25 vs local 1.x drift (CI ran 0.25.3, deadlocking on the StaticPool sqlite connection) → bumped to ^1.3; :memory:/StaticPool shared across loops → file-backed sqlite + NullPool; plus the WS bug. Not Linux-specific, despite first appearances.
  • Gates armed. pr-validation runs the full suite; backend-ci drops || true for agent-engine only (others unaudited, trainer-service ~97 known failures) and now installs Poetry dev groups properly.
  • Honest limits. Two org_id tests skipped as Postgres-only rather than relaxed; session-scoped loop scope rejected because it breaks two tests relying on per-test isolation.

[2026-08-06] — Summit goal discovery grounded in real PRISM; Goals menu restored for the owner

Restoring the Goals shortcut surfaced a much larger defect underneath it: the goal-discovery flow it leads to had never been PRISM-grounded in either deployed environment, despite documenting that it was. Merged to development: FE #374 (3e429aa4), BE #819 (d19cdacc).

  • The grounding was dead on both tiers. _prism_context read through retrieve_personal_context, which returns "" outright when deterministic_personalization is on — it is true on dev, so every ask/synthesize ran with (none on file). On staging-b the flag is false, so the same call fell through to the legacy uploader-keyed document search: the 2026-07-12 cross-subject contamination vector, capped at 500 tokens of arbitrary chunks, and not a source of structured scores in any case. The chat path was never affected — GoalAgent extends BaseAgent, which injects the real <USER_PROFILE>; only the structured UI calls bypassed it by hitting provider.chat directly.
  • Synthesis was fabricating the alignment. With no profile in the prompt, the model was still asked for a prism_alignment — and produced a quadrant, a dimension list and an execution style, invented whole. Goals were shown as PRISM-aligned when the alignment was imaginary: wrong in a way the reader cannot check.
  • P0 — grounding. Reads now use the structured profile platform (load_user_profile_block_for_chat), the same path routes/interview.py uses: plain SQL over assessments/assessment_scores plus the user's own doc_kind-tagged résumé and bio, no embeddings, unaffected by the flag by design. It also brings in facts, any non-PRISM instrument, and the chat_excluded_frameworks privacy filter the pgvector path ignored. The WHY ladder gets the profile too.
  • P0 — honesty. _sanitise_alignment discards any behavioural claim the profile does not support: no profile → null alignment and null execution style; unknown dimensions dropped; if none survive the whole alignment goes; invalid enum values dropped rather than passed through. The synthesis prompt is now conditional (explicitly instructing null and forbidding inference), so the sanitiser is a backstop rather than the only defence. /synthesize returns hasPrism.
  • P1 — score type pinned to Underlying. Dev stores three variants of every BehaviorPreferences dimension — Underlying 150 rows, Adapted 124, Consistent 124 — which disagree by design; unfiltered reads mixed all three. Filtering required the loader to project score_type, which it never did, so Underlying and Adapted were indistinguishable to every consumer. ScoreView now carries it as an optional additive field. Legacy NULL-typed rows are used only when no Underlying exists; Adapted is never substituted.
  • P1 — quadrant mapping pinned to app/prism_canon.py. The PRISM brief renders deterministically under the licensed-manual grouping (Blue = Supporting + Co-Ordinating, Gold = Finishing + Evaluating), and a goal's quadrant is derived from its surviving dimensions rather than accepted from the model — so Summit cannot reintroduce the rotation that made Supporting/Co-Ordinating the wrong colour in three other places. Output passes normalise_colour_names; PRISM has four colours and Orange is not one.
  • Goals menu — owner only. Restored for [email redacted]; every other user's menu is byte-identical to 2026-08-04. getUserNavItems takes the viewer's email so the rule lives in one place (isPlatformOwner) and omitting it fails closed; all three chromes pass it. Deliberately not added to OWNER_ONLY_NAV_ROUTES (that set removes rows, which would change what others see), and the row keeps its position so the gate cannot reshuffle anyone's menu. A shortcut gate, not an access gate — the route was never removed and Goals stayed reachable via the Direction Setting sub-nav and JourneyPage stage 5.
  • Verified — backend 4535 passed vs 4511 on base, with a byte-identical set of 174 pre-existing failures (test_websocket, test_ws_handler, test_history_token_budget), confirmed by diffing failure lists with the change stashed: no regressions, 24 new tests. Frontend 135 tests green, npm run build clean, eslint clean on changed files — and the pre-existing greyed-Goals assertions pass unchanged, which is the evidence nobody else's menu moved.

Path to green

  • Aspect fix (commit e99f9e8): UniqueRouteKeyAspect.visit was deduping by routeKey alone despite docstring promising (apiId, routeKey). Caused false-positive synth error: WS-API $default vs HTTP-API $default. Bucketed seen routes by resolved apiId Map-of-Maps; cross-stack same-API collision detection (the 2026-05-15 /v1/organizations class) is preserved.
  • Default-ref trap caught: gh workflow run cdk-deploy.yml without --ref development defaulted to main (3-week-old SHA 880411cd) → first deploy attempt synthed stale Wave 7 routes still in source → CREATE conflict with live → rollback wiped the pre-compact v2 IMPORT of SFRouteDefaultCatchall.
  • Recovery IMPORT v3 (adopt-default-route-2026-06-16-v3): hand-crafted change-set against the live template added SFRouteDefaultCatchall with DeletionPolicy:Retain, mapped to live route q5w9oa2. IMPORT_COMPLETE.
  • Deploy from development ref: re-dispatched with --ref development. Synth + diff + deploy all clean. No resource creates/deletes.

Lesson earned

  • After a failed CFN deploy + rollback that included imported resources, CFN can drop those imports during cleanup. Always verify imports survived with describe-stack-resources --logical-resource-id <X> before re-running deploy.
  • The repo's default branch is main, not development. Any gh workflow run needs explicit --ref development for CDK deploys.

Known follow-up — filename discriminator gap

The /v1/documents/latest-prism endpoint matches PRISM CSVs via doc_kind = 'prism' OR (LOWER(filename) LIKE '%prism%' AND LOWER(filename) LIKE '%.csv'). The doc_kind='prism' branch is forward-compat — no current ingestion code path writes that value (always 'general'). Two known failure modes for the working filename branch:

  1. User uploaded via the generic /v1/documents/upload flow with a filename that doesn't contain "prism" — endpoint returns 404, auto-attach silently no-ops, user manually attaches via the new Documents dropdown.
  2. User imported via /v1/agents/documents/import-prism — that endpoint parses + discards the file (ingestion.py:360) and only persists parsed scores into prism_results + vector store. No documents row exists for the endpoint to find.

Mitigation candidates for a follow-up PR: have /import-prism persist a documents row with doc_kind='prism'; OR have the endpoint fall back to prism_results + synthesize a document_id.

Ships runbook + non-interactive cdk import wrapper at infrastructure/cdk/cdk-import/. Not auto-executed; shared-infra change requires explicit operator action.

T3 — Fix chat_message_repository.insert asyncpg codec bug (PR #330 draft, blocked on T21 48h soak)

  • Root cause: ws_handler.py:241 — session_id = body.get("session_id") or connection_id falls back to API GW connectionId (base64-shaped token like ecR3ucRzoAMCEWw=, not a UUID) when client omits session_id. asyncpg rejects after network round-trip; WS handler swallows as non-fatal; chat history row silently drops. 12 dropped turns / 6 sessions / 24h on Dev.
  • Two-pronged fix: upstream (ws_handler.py) validates UUID-parseable session_id and mints uuid4 fallback otherwise + repository guard validates uuid.UUID(session_id) before any DB touch, raising InvalidChatMessageError ("not a valid UUID — looks like a connection_id?") with bad value in message.

  • Draft — gated on T21 48h soak. 24h post-deploy zero-insert-failure soak before T22 unblocks.

[2026-05-16] — Aura DISC interpreter (Phase 1 of behavioral framework overlays)

First of five planned framework overlays for Aura, per the Behavioral Assessment Interpretation Manual (May 2026) §6.1 Agent Architecture and §6.7 build sequence. Aura now ingests a DISC report from SharedContext, runs the §1.4 pattern-recognition rules (12 classical patterns, intensity bands, ≥15-pt stress-shift detection, flat-profile refusal, hiring-decision refusal), publishes a structured DISCInterpretation back to SharedContext for downstream agents (Meridian synthesis, Atlas team rollups, Nova role-fit, James Job-Blueprint signals, Forge interpersonal coaching), and conditionally injects a keyword-routed <DISC_REFERENCE> block into her system prompt — same pattern as prism_knowledge.py.

Added

  • services/agent-engine/app/agents/coaching/frameworks/__init__.py — package init with FrameworkInterpretation Pydantic base and runtime-checkable InterpreterProtocol.
  • services/agent-engine/app/agents/coaching/frameworks/disc_knowledge.py — 11 enum-keyed sections (SCORE_BANDS, DIM_D/I/S/C, CLASSICAL_PATTERNS, STRESS_SHIFT, COMMUNICATION, EDGE_CASES, REFUSAL_BOUNDARIES, PRISM_MAPPING); keyword-routed select_sections() + budget-aware render_sections() capped at ~2200 tokens. REFUSAL_BOUNDARIES is non-droppable so selection-decision guardrails always survive.
  • services/agent-engine/app/agents/coaching/frameworks/disc_interpreter.py — DISCReport/DISCScores (§1.2 Input Data Schema), DISCInterpretation (§1.5 Output Schema), interpret() implementing §1.4 pattern rules + per-style communication preferences + confidence calibration per §6.3.
  • services/agent-engine/app/agents/coaching/frameworks/reconciliation.py — disc_to_prism(D|I|S|C) live (PRISM-canon mapping). bigfive_to_prism, mbti_to_prism, clifton_to_prism, enneagram_to_prism all raise NotImplementedError per §6.2 — no silent partial blends until each interpreter ships.
  • services/agent-engine/tests/agents/coaching/frameworks/ — 75 net-new tests: test_disc_knowledge.py (26), test_disc_interpreter.py (43), test_aura_wiring.py (6). All green.

Discrepancy Noted (for source-doc follow-up)

The source manual's §1.8 DISC→PRISM mapping labels D as "Gold (Initiating)" and C as "Green (Finishing) + Orange (Focusing)" — contradicts both the canonical PRISM quadrants in prism_knowledge.py (Green = Innovating+Initiating, Blue = Supporting+Co-Ordinating, Red = Focusing+Delivering [Orange synonym], Gold = Finishing+Evaluating) and standard Wiley/TTI cross-framework mappings. Per §6.2 "PRISM wins, surface the discrepancy," ships with PRISM-canon mapping (D→Red/Focusing, I→Green/Initiating, S→Blue/Supporting, C→Gold/Finishing). Source §1.8 should be corrected in a follow-up.

[2026-05-16] — PR3 of RAG plan §8: post-deploy probes in cdk-deploy.yml

Third of the 10 permanent-fix PRs from RAG_RELIABILITY_PLAN.md §8. Adds 6 bash probe scripts + a new post-deploy-probes job in cdk-deploy.yml that fails the CDK Deploy workflow when any of the 5 RAG-pipeline regression classes are detected post-deploy. Breaks the cycle of "I hot-patch, you redeploy, it breaks again."

Added

  • scripts/post-deploy-probes/lib.sh — shared catalog (RAG Lambdas, buckets, SGs, endpoints, sentinels)
  • 01-bucket-cors.sh — bucket CORS drift detection
  • 02-lambda-vpc.sh — Lambda VPC config strip detection
  • 03-sg-egress-ingress.sh — bidirectional SG topology check (catches the 2026-05-16 egress regression)
  • 04-endpoint-health.sh — probes 8 endpoints for HTTP < 500 in < 10s
  • 05-lambda-bundle-sentinels.sh — verifies deployed Lambda zips contain post-fix sentinel strings
  • 06-api-gw-route-uniqueness.sh — runtime version of UniqueRouteKeyAspect (catches console-added dups)
  • run-all.sh — top-level runner
  • .github/workflows/cdk-deploy.yml — new post-deploy-probes job after verify-no-stubs

Verified

  • All 6 probes run locally: 4 pass, 2 correctly catch known issues (observability 500 + 4 dup routes — both skip-listed pending fixes)
  • Bash 3.2 compatible (refactored from declare -A)

Why this is the long-term fix

PR1 (#144) + PR2 (#145) codify the 2026-05-15/16 specific drift bugs. PR3 catches ANY future regression of the same 5 classes at deploy time, BEFORE users see it. Without PR3, every CDK deploy is a roll of the dice on whether services-stack drift surfaces a new outage.

[2026-05-14] — P1-9 meta-conversation intent: memory recall bypasses specialists (PR #108)

Wave E item P1-9 — fixes Bug B from IG_Meridian_Routing_Examples_2026-05-13.docx Example 3. The original misroute: "do you remember past responses — give a brief summary" was hijacked by Echo (SessionAgent) because "remember" / "reflection" / "session" / "summary" all match its capabilities=["feedback-collection", "reflection"]. The fix introduces a meta_conversation intent class detected BEFORE the specialist classifier runs, so memory-recall and summary requests are answered directly by Meridian using the short-term memory transcript.

    • _META_CONVERSATION_PATTERNS — 14 regex patterns covering documented meta phrasings ("do you remember", "summarize our conversation", "what did we discuss", "recap", "tl;dr", "remind me what we covered", "your previous response", etc.)
    • _META_CONVERSATION_REGEX — compiled once at module load, case-insensitive
    • _count_meta_conversation_hits() — counts distinct pattern matches
    • _is_meta_conversation() — dominance-checks meta hits against the top single-domain keyword score so "remember to follow up about my PRISM profile" still routes to coaching
    • Meridian._handle_meta_conversation() — direct LLM call with system prompt + transcript of last 30 short-term messages; gracefully handles empty history with a "we're just getting started" copy (no LLM call)
    • Wired into both Meridian.respond() (REST) and Meridian.route() (streaming) BEFORE sticky routing
    • Explicit @agent invocation always overrides meta routing
    • logger.info("meta_conversation_routing_applied ...") on every fire — CloudWatch auditable
  • services/agent-engine/tests/test_meridian_meta_conversation.py — 64 new tests covering detector unit tests (22 meta phrasings + 7 domain counter-examples), parametrized pattern coverage (25 documented phrases), end-to-end Meridian.respond() with non-empty history / empty history / sticky-routing override / explicit-invocation override / incidental-keyword false positive, the Example 3 regression replay, and the streaming path.

Fixed — [email redacted]

  • Cognito: deleted (he was stuck in RESET_REQUIRED since 2026-05-12, blocking the password-reset path that auth-service uses).
  • Magic-Auth (inspires_genius.magic_auth.users): inserted via POST /api/auth/add-user, user_id [uuid], role user, is_active=true, email_verified=true.
  • Canonical (inspire_genius.public.users): inserted with the SAME user_id so the agent-engine canonical-sub remap (PR #93) is a no-op for him; auth_provider=cognito (the enum has no magic_link value yet — kept for consistency with existing rows). No user_profiles/org_users linkage; "IG" organisation was not created.

Fixed — chat document upload was broken for ALL users since 2026-05-09

  • Symptom: every browser-direct presigned POST silently failed (file never landed in S3) while the document-service Lambda happily wrote a DB row + returned a presigned URL. Accumulated 42 orphan documents with file_size=0 status=pending across 9 different user_ids.
  • Root cause: ig-dev-documents bucket had no CORS configuration, so the browser blocked every cross-origin POST. The other bucket inspires-genius-dev-documents (used by the monolith bridge, server-to-server, no browser CORS) had CORS and worked — that's why wesley's CV PDF actually went through that path on 2026-05-12 but his chat uploads didn't.
  • Live hotfix: aws s3api put-bucket-cors on ig-dev-documents with scoped origins (https://dev.inspiresgenius.com, both CloudFront aliases, http://localhost:5173) matching magic-auth's FRONTEND_ORIGINS env. Methods POST/GET/HEAD/PUT. Preflight verified live.
  • CDK durability: infrastructure/cdk/lib/services-stack.ts:704 — added cors: block to the DocumentsBucket definition with the same scope. Without it the next cdk deploy would synth a template without the rule and silently revert the hotfix. PR #98 opened against development.
  • Orphan cleanup: 42 public.documents rows deleted (file_size=0 AND status='pending' AND s3_bucket='ig-dev-documents'). Zero document_chunks attached — no recoverable data; affected users need to re-upload.

Known follow-ups

  • auth_provider_enum has no magic_link value. Wesley is tagged cognito to fit the existing enum. If we want to track auth source accurately, that's an ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE migration.
  • Magic-Auth ⇄ canonical sub mismatch from PR #93 still affects older users whose Magic-Auth user_id ≠ public.users.user_id (will's 7 docs under 346854a8-…). PR #93 remaps JWT sub going forward; historical rows stay where they were written.

[2026-05-13] — User Management top-to-bottom review (no code changes yet)

Triggered by an operator question: "There are a number of users whose status is deactivated, but I can't delete them from the list. Why can't they be purged?"

Root cause (the dead end)

delete_user_by_email() in inspire-genius-backend/users/auth_service/schema.py:741-873 returns success: false, "User is already deactivated" whenever user.is_deleted = True. There is no hard-delete branch for soft-deleted users, no force flag, and no separate purge endpoint. The frontend "Purge inactive users" button (user-management.service.ts:178-223) iterates inactive emails through this same endpoint, so every call is refused and the rows persist. Soft-delete is hit on the first click; second click is permanently rejected.

Other issues found

  • FK landmine for future fix: issues.reported_by and organization_agents.assigned_by are NO ACTION (implicit RESTRICT). A force-purge of real soft-deleted users will trip this. Fix: Alembic migration to ON DELETE SET NULL + null those columns before delete.
  • Cognito drift on soft delete: only update_cognito_user_attributes(is_active=False) is called; the account itself is not disabled. admin_disable_user is missing.
  • Audit log gap: useUserManagement.ts logs actor_email: "admin" as a literal string, not the calling super-admin.
  • Type mismatch: DeleteUserData.deletion_type declares 'soft_delete' but backend returns "invitation_only".
  • Three overlapping invite paths: monolith single, monolith bulk, microservice DynamoDB+SES. Frontend uses only the single monolith path.
  • Orphaned services/user-service/: full CRUD built, frontend never calls it. Also defines a different user_profiles schema than the monolith (collision waiting to happen).
  • Company-admin Users page is a stub: /api/company/users doesn't exist.
  • UserManagement.tsx bulk-delete reimplements the purge logic instead of reusing the hook (~700 LOC page).

Recommended fix (~2-3 hours)

  • Extend DELETE /v1/user-management/users/{email} to accept ?force=true — super-admin only — that hard-deletes already-soft-deleted users.
  • New POST /v1/user-management/users/purge-inactive (server-side transactional fanout) to replace the client-side Promise.allSettled loop.
  • Alembic migration: ALTER ... ON DELETE SET NULL on issues.reported_by + organization_agents.assigned_by.
  • Add cognito_client.admin_disable_user() to the soft-delete branch; keep admin_delete_user() for force-purge.
  • Frontend: relabel row action to "Permanently delete" for deactivated rows, call deleteUserByEmail(email, true); "Purge inactive" header button hits the new server endpoint.
  • Fix actor_email to read from AuthContext; rename "invitation_only" → "soft_delete".

Why no code yet

This is a /bedtime review only. The original author chose the audit-safety stance (no hard-delete of verified users); the patch reverses that for super-admin via a force flag, which is a product decision worth confirming before shipping. Full patch sketch + verification curl is in USER_MANAGEMENT_REVIEW_2026-05-13.md.

  • inspire-genius-backend/users/auth_service/schema.py:741-873
  • inspire-genius-backend/users/auth_service/user_management.py
  • inspire-genius-frontend/src/services/super-admin/user-management/user-management.service.ts
  • inspire-genius-frontend/src/hooks/super-admin/user-management/useUserManagement.ts
  • inspire-genius-frontend/src/pages/super-admin/UserManagement.tsx

/full-go r-2.6 autonomous run. Verdict: PASS. RBAC is correctly implemented + tested across the agent engine; no code changes required.

Key findings

  • 6-role hierarchy in app/permissions/roles.py with is_at_least() helper + named-permission map. 33 dedicated tests pass.
  • Role propagation: JWT → auth_deps.require_auth → AgentContext(role=...) at both REST and WS (handlers.py:213, 458) entry points.
  • 5/5 gated specialist agents enforce role: Ascend (manager+), Maven (manager/practitioner/admin), Sentinel (company-admin+), Anchor (super-admin + practitioner), Nexus (super-admin + practitioner).
  • James/AdminAgent dual-tier: gated at orchestrator level via business_orchestrator._is_admin_query + _ADMIN_ROLES — by design (James also serves Job Blueprint career-fit for all roles).
  • Structured denial: AgentResponse.metadata = {access_denied: True, required_roles: [...]}. EventBridge emits agent.admin.access_denied.
  • Tool-level RBAC + per-role quotas in app/permissions/tool_access.py + quotas.py.

Test verification (no live token-minting needed)

  • tests/test_permissions.py + test_audit_agent.py: 65/65 PASS
  • tests/test_orchestrators.py -k "access_denied or role": 4/4 PASS
  • test_mcp_tools.py + test_roles_analytics.py + test_debug_rag.py::test_require_super_admin_rejects_lower_roles: 73/74 PASS (1 unrelated email-tool failure)
  • Total RBAC-relevant: 69+ tests passing, 0 RBAC failures

Why R-2.2 saw "0/3 strict pass" on RBAC denials

The R-2.2 matcher scanned response.content for keywords like "denied"/"forbidden". Agents use polite natural-language phrasing; the structural signal lives in response.metadata.access_denied (boolean). R-2.2 fix (no agent-engine change): switch matcher to response.metadata.get("access_denied") is True. Flips RBAC sub-score 0/3 → expected 3/3.

Quality delta within multi-agent: M1 went from single-node [Forge] to genuine multi-node [Compass, Forge] — the few-shot pattern is firing. Strict gate still fails because LLM picked Compass instead of Aura.

Architectural finding — strict 24/24 needs cross-orchestrator coordination

M1, M2, M3 expectations require agents from two different domains:

  • M1: Aura (coaching) + Forge (business)
  • M2: Atlas (business) + Echo (coaching)
  • M3: Sentinel (system) + Sage (business)
  • M4: Grant + Bridge — both in career_talent → passes ✅

Today's architecture routes each message to one domain orchestrator whose Planner only sees that domain's agents. No amount of prompt tightening can produce [Aura, Forge] from a single planner call — Aura is not in Business's agent list and Forge is not in Coaching's. Strict 24/24 acceptance for M1/M2/M3 requires a Meridian-level multi-domain coordinator that fans a compound prompt into two single-domain orchestrator calls and re-synthesises the result. Recommend treating this as a new R-2.2-followup rung (or folding into Phase G).

  • Reproduced cleanly in 5-event burst after stub fix: RuntimeError: Event loop is closed from asyncpg pool recycling pinned connections.

[2026-05-10] — Cross-session conversational continuity + catch-all session log

Closes the cross-session memory gap surfaced by the 2026-05-09 audit: returning users now see their prior conversation history (not just structured insights), and the session log fires on every turn instead of only on farewell keywords.

Agent Engine — services/agent-engine/app/memory/

  • short_term.py — added get_recent_messages_across_sessions(user_id, exclude_session_id, message_limit, session_limit). Two-query implementation: one to find recent session_ids (excluding the current one), one to pull their messages.
  • manager.py:
    • recall() now accepts include_prior_sessions, prior_session_message_limit, prior_session_count, prior_session_summary_limit. When enabled, the short-term tier additionally returns prior_sessions + prior_summaries.
    • consolidate() now accepts clear_working: bool = True. When False, the summary + insights are persisted but the session's working-memory namespace is preserved — the path used for incremental, every-turn consolidation.
  • integration.py:
    • load_context() now defaults to include_prior_sessions=True and surfaces a new prior_session_history key plus expanded session_summaries (current + prior).
    • format_memory_block() renders cross-session continuity inside <USER_MEMORY> as a new <prior_conversations> block (grouped by session_id, with <turn role="…"> children, per-message char cap + XML escaping) and a <session_summaries> block carrying a session= attribute. Token-budget-aware.
    • summarize_session() threads clear_working through to MemoryManager.consolidate().

Agent Engine — services/agent-engine/app/agents/meridian.py

  • Both respond() (REST) and route() (streaming) now call summarize_session(..., clear_working=is_farewell) on every turn. The session log is no longer keyword-gated — detect_farewell() only decides whether to flip clear_working=True and whether to fire the session_ended EventBridge event + observability finalisation.
  • Net effect: insights from sessions where the user does not say "goodbye" are no longer lost when the 7-day short-term retention expires; the running summary is durable from turn 1.

Tests

  • tests/test_memory_integration.py — added TestCrossSessionHistory (6 tests: prior sessions excluded by current sid, summary aggregation, opt-out, rendering, XML escaping, truncation) and TestClearWorkingFlag (3 tests: default clear, opt-out preserves working memory, summarize_session threads the flag). 57/57 passing.
  • tests/test_meridian.py — TestFarewellDetection rewritten to reflect the new contract: every turn calls summarize_session() with clear_working mirroring farewell detection; emit_session_ended only fires on farewell. 4 tests, all passing.
  • Full memory + meridian sweep: 180/180 passing. Broader agent-engine sweep introduces 0 new failures (delta vs origin/development = 0 tests).

Behavioral impact for end users (post-deploy)

A returning user will now see, in addition to PRISM scores / goals / corrections / preferences:

  • Transcript snippets of their prior sessions (capped, attributed to their session_id).
  • A list of session summaries from prior sessions (with timestamps + session_ids).
  • Insights extracted from sessions that ended without an explicit farewell — previously lost when short-term expired.

[2026-05-08] — P4 (Phase D R3) canary flipped on dev: chat_message writer = agent-engine

Changed

Operationalised the Phase D R3 chat_message writer migration that PR #37 had shipped as code. After flipping the canary flag, all new chat-message rows on dev are written by services/agent-engine/app/repositories/chat_message_repository.py instead of the monolith add_message_to_conversation.

Steps performed

  • Migration applied — phase_d_chat_writer_canary.sql invoked via aws lambda invoke ig-dev-migration-runner. Idempotent ALTER added chat_messages.writer VARCHAR(32) NULL plus the helper idx_chat_messages_writer_created_at index.
  • Inventory clean — 7-day SELECT returned 0 rows; no unknown writers in the canary window.
  • Image rebuilt — services/agent-engine Docker image rebuilt for linux/amd64 and pushed to ECR with both latest and phase-d-r3 tags. Manifest digest sha256:6e4f88357e48.... The previous latest was from 2026-05-06, predating PR #37.
  • Task-def rev 34 deployed — registered with AGENT_ENGINE_CHAT_MESSAGE_WRITER=agent-engine. Earlier rev 33 used the unprefixed name CHAT_MESSAGE_WRITER, which silently fell through to the "monolith" default because pydantic-settings on Settings uses env_prefix="AGENT_ENGINE_". ECS Exec into the running rev-34 task confirmed settings.chat_message_writer == 'agent-engine'.
  • CDK persisted — infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts now sets AGENT_ENGINE_CHAT_MESSAGE_WRITER (overridable via --context chatMessageWriter=monolith for emergency rollback).
  • Monolith writer guard — inspire-genius-backend/ai/chat_services/chat_schema.py::add_message_to_conversation now reads MONOLITH_CHAT_WRITER_ENABLED (default "true"). When set to "false"/"0"/"no" the function returns None without inserting. After the 24h canary closes the operator flips this env var to disable the legacy writer in a single change, no code redeploy.
  • migration-runner improvement — services/migration-runner/handler.py now returns the per-statement results list inside the response body so SELECT verification queries surface row data without tailing CloudWatch logs.

Acceptance (this PR)

  • ✅ Migration column + index visible in dev DB
  • ✅ Fresh ECR image built + pushed; ECS task-def rev 34 running with the right env-var name
  • ✅ settings.chat_message_writer == 'agent-engine' confirmed inside the running container
  • ✅ Monolith writer guard ships at default "true" → no behaviour change today
  • ⏸ 24h canary observation + monolith hard-removal (steps 11-12 of the Monday plan) remain a follow-up

Process note (worth remembering)

pydantic-settings env prefixes silently demote unprefixed env vars to defaults. The first task-def revision used CHAT_MESSAGE_WRITER; pydantic ignored it and the container reported 'monolith'. Always grep the Settings class for env_prefix before naming new env vars, and prefer ECS Exec + from app.config import settings; print(...) over reading task-def JSON to verify a flip actually landed.

[2026-05-03] — fix: Backend CI docker-scan recovery (all 9 services green)

Fixed

  • CI workflow build context — workflow always used service-dir context for docker build, but 5 service Dockerfiles (coach, dashboard, org, support, user) were authored for repo-root context. Added a grep-based detector that picks the right context per Dockerfile. Files: .github/workflows/backend-ci.yml
  • Pre-commit detect-secrets version mismatch — .pre-commit-config.yaml pinned v1.4.0 but .secrets.baseline referenced v1.5.0-only plugins (GitLab/IPPublic/OpenAI/Pypi/Telegram detectors). Bumped pin to v1.5.0. Files: .pre-commit-config.yaml
  • ig-auth path-dep break in 6 service Dockerfiles — pyproject.toml declares ig-auth = {path = "../../packages/ig-auth"}. With no committed poetry.lock, the builder's poetry export re-resolved deps and looked for /packages/ig-auth (relative to WORKDIR /build) — not present. Generated and committed poetry.lock for all 6 services (force-added past .gitignore). Added sed -i '/^-e .*ig.auth/d' requirements.txt after export so the path-dep line doesn't break the runtime stage's pip install -r requirements.txt; ig-auth is installed separately via pip install /tmp/ig-auth/. Files: services/{auth,support,coach,dashboard,org,user}-service/Dockerfile + poetry.lock
  • auth-service Dockerfile rewrite — old version used service-dir context with no ig-auth handling, relying entirely on stale Docker layer cache. Rewritten to match the repo-root pattern of the other 5. Files: services/auth-service/Dockerfile

Result

  • All 9 docker-scan jobs in Backend CI — Services Security & Tests now pass on development (run 25270872174). Previously 6 of 9 were chronically failing on layer-cache-masked path-dep errors.

CLAUDE.md root/CLAUDE.md

Project Overview

Inspire Genius is an AI coaching platform frontend. The app code lives entirely in inspire-genius-frontend/. There is a Python venv/ at the repo root (not related to the frontend).

Commands (from inspire-genius-frontend/)

  • npm run dev — Start Vite dev server
  • npm run build — TypeScript check + Vite production build
  • npm run lint — ESLint
  • npm run test — Jest in watch mode
  • npm run test:ci — Jest single run (CI)
  • npm run test:coverage — Jest with coverage report

Stack

React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7 + Tailwind CSS 4 + shadcn/ui (new-york style, slate base)

Data Flow Pattern

Service → Hook → Component

  • Services (src/services/): Axios calls organized by domain (auth, coaches, documents, help, onboarding, super-admin, alex/chat, user)
  • Hooks (src/hooks/): React Query mutations/queries wrapping services. Server state via TanStack React Query.
  • Pages (src/pages/): Route-level components organized by role (auth, onboarding, user, manager, company-admin, practitioner, distributor, super-admin, legal)

Global State

React Context only (no Redux/Zustand)

  • AuthContext — auth lifecycle, token management, role-based navigation
  • TourContext — guided tour with audio narration
  • SidebarContext — sidebar UI state

Routing (src/routes.tsx)

  • Public: /login, /signup, /otp, /forgot, /reset-password, /accept-invitation, /social-login, /terms, /privacy
  • User: /home, /dashboard, /coaches, /documents, /settings, /help, /onboarding/*
  • Manager: /manager/*
  • Company Admin: /company-admin/*
  • Practitioner: /practitioner/*
  • Distributor: /distributor/*
  • Super Admin: /super-admin/*
  • ProtectedRoute enforces auth, role checks, and onboarding completion

Six User Roles (defined in src/constants/routes.ts as ROLES enum)

  • user — end user / employee receiving coaching
  • manager — supervisory role with direct-report visibility
  • company-admin — organization-level administrator
  • practitioner — PRISM-accredited coach, uses IG as business platform
  • distributor — regional wholesaler of PRISM credits to Practitioners
  • super-admin — platform owner, full access

API Layer (src/lib/axios.ts)

  • Singleton axios instance, base URL from VITE_API_BASE_URL env var (default http://localhost:3000)
  • Request interceptor injects access-token from encrypted storage
  • Response interceptor handles 401 with single-flight token refresh, auto-retry, or logout

Auth Storage

src/lib/secureStorage.ts + src/lib/storage.ts — sensitive data (tokens) via encrypted storage wrapper. Keys centralized in STORAGE_KEYS enum.

UI Components

src/components/ui/: shadcn/ui library. Add new components via npx shadcn@latest add <component>. Path alias @/ maps to src/.

Testing

Jest + jsdom + React Testing Library, tests colocated in __tests__/ directories. CSS modules mocked via identity-obj-proxy.

Microservices (services/)

Phase 2 Strangler Fig extraction — endpoints migrated from monolith to independent Lambda-backed microservices.

Auth Service (services/auth-service/) — Status: Extracted

  • FastAPI + Mangum Lambda microservice (31 files)
  • 12 endpoints: login, signup, verify-otp, resend-otp, forgot-password, reset-password, refresh-token, logout, magic-auth, validate-token, me, health
  • Dual JWT: RS256 (Cognito) + HS256 (Magic Auth)
  • DynamoDB rate limiting: 5 attempts / IP / 15 min
  • EventBridge events: auth.user.login, auth.user.signup, auth.user.logout, auth.token.refresh
  • Commands: uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8001, pytest tests/ -v

CDK Infrastructure (infrastructure/cdk/)

  • Lambda Concurrency — Reserved per function (Auth=100, Audit=50, Phase 5=50, RLHF=25); provisioned concurrency in prod (Auth 10, Audit 5 warm)
  • DynamoDB Scaling — PAY_PER_REQUEST in dev/staging; PROVISIONED + auto-scaling at 70% target in prod
  • ECS Scheduled Scaling — Business hours 8am-8pm EST weekdays: prod min 5, staging min 3; off-hours min 2
  • API Gateway Throttling — prod 1000/500, staging 500/250, dev 100/50; per-route throttling on auth endpoints
  • CloudWatch Alarms — 33 alarms: Lambda duration/errors/throttles (10 functions) + 3 Aurora alarms (CPU, connections, ACU)
  • CDK Conventions — use tryBundle stubs for local synth; avoid reserved AWS env var names

Key Conventions

  • Route constants in src/constants/routes.ts (ROUTES, ROLES, STORAGE_KEYS, NEXT_STEPS)
  • Forms use React Hook Form + Zod validation
  • Notifications via Sonner toast (<Toaster> in App.tsx)
  • Icons from lucide-react
  • Path alias: @/ → src/ (configured in Vite, tsconfig, and jest)
  • After making notable changes, update change_log.md and IG_project_log.html
  • After every user prompt, append it to the session_prompts section in IG_project_log.html

Project Documentation

  • change_log.md — chronological record of all project changes
  • database_schema.md — frontend data models and API entity schemas
  • IG_project_log.html — standalone HTML dashboard with all docs + session prompt history
  • .claude/rules/ — development rules (code-style, architecture, workflow, session-logging)
  • Project Log page available at /super-admin/project-log in the app

Global Session Behavior

Automatic Logging: Every session automatically logs activity to IG_project_log.html and change_log.md via deterministic hooks.

Hooks (.claude/settings.json)

  • UserPromptSubmit → logs prompt to session_prompts section
  • PostToolUse (Edit/Write) → logs file modifications to session_activity + change_log.md
  • Stop → logs session end

Python Hook Script

.claude/hooks/update_project_log.py — standalone Python 3 script (no pip dependencies) that updates HTML log entries, increments prompt count badge, appends to change_log.md, and syncs all copy locations.

Slash Commands

  • /log-session — summarize and log current session's changes to both log files
  • /sync-logs — sync IG_project_log.html and change_log.md to all copy locations
  • /project-status — show recent project activity summary
  • /bedtime — end-of-day session wrap-up with full doc sync
  • /doc-update — full documentation update across all files and copy locations

Log File Locations (keep in sync)

  • ./IG_project_log.html (project root — primary)
  • ./inspire-genius-frontend/public/IG_project_log.html (served by Vite/S3)
  • ./inspire-genius-frontend/IG_project_log.html (frontend root copy)
  • ./change_log.md (project root — primary)
  • ./inspire-genius-frontend/change_log.md (frontend copy)

Code Style Rules .claude/rules/code-style.md

TypeScript

  • Strict TypeScript; avoid any — use proper types from src/types/
  • Use type for object shapes, interface only when extending
  • Prefer named exports for components, default exports for pages

React

  • Functional components only
  • React Hook Form + Zod for forms
  • TanStack React Query for server state
  • Context for global state only (auth, tour, sidebar)

Styling

  • Tailwind CSS utilities only — no CSS modules
  • cn() from @/lib/utils for conditional classes
  • shadcn/ui from @/components/ui/
  • lucide-react icons exclusively

File Organization

  • Pages: src/pages/{auth,onboarding,user,super-admin,legal}/
  • Tests: __tests__/ next to source
  • Services: src/services/ by domain
  • Hooks: src/hooks/ by domain
  • Types: src/types/ by domain

Architecture Rules .claude/rules/architecture.md

Data Flow

Service → Hook → Component (never call services from components directly)

API Layer

  • All HTTP via singleton axios in src/lib/axios.ts
  • Token injection & 401 refresh handled by interceptors
  • Responses follow BaseApiResponse<T> envelope

Auth

  • AuthContext manages auth lifecycle
  • useAuth() hook for auth state
  • ProtectedRoute enforces roles
  • Six roles: user, manager, company-admin, practitioner, distributor, super-admin
  • Encrypted storage for tokens

Routing

  • All routes in src/routes.tsx using useRoutes
  • Constants in src/constants/routes.ts
  • Role-specific route groups: /manager/*, /company-admin/*, /practitioner/*, /distributor/*, /super-admin/*
  • User pages → UserLayout, role layouts are thin wrappers around AppShell
  • Nav items per role in src/constants/navigation.ts (NAV_ITEMS_BY_ROLE)

Layouts

  • AppShell — unified 3-column layout (sidebar | main | right panel) used by ALL roles
  • Role-specific layouts (ManagerLayout, CompanyAdminLayout, PractitionerLayout, DistributorLayout, SuperAdminLayout, UserLayout)

Session Hooks & Commands

  • Deterministic hooks in .claude/settings.json fire on UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop events
  • Hook script .claude/hooks/update_project_log.py auto-logs session activity
  • Slash commands: /log-session, /sync-logs, /project-status, /bedtime, /doc-update

Microservices (services/)

  • Strangler Fig pattern: endpoints extracted from monolith into Lambda-backed FastAPI + Mangum services
  • Auth Service (services/auth-service/): 12 endpoints, dual JWT (RS256 + HS256), DynamoDB rate limiting, EventBridge events
  • Each microservice gets: Lambda, IAM role, CloudWatch alarms, API Gateway routes in services-stack.ts
  • Rate limiting via DynamoDB with TTL auto-cleanup
  • EventBridge for cross-service events (e.g. auth.user.login triggers audit)

CDK Infrastructure Conventions

  • Always add reservedConcurrentExecutions to new Lambda functions
  • Always add CloudWatch alarms (duration, errors, throttles) for new Lambdas
  • Use tryBundle local stubs for Docker-less CDK synth
  • Avoid reserved AWS env var names (e.g. use AWS_REGION_OVERRIDE not AWS_REGION)
  • DynamoDB: PAY_PER_REQUEST in dev, PROVISIONED + auto-scaling in prod
  • API Gateway: environment-dependent throttle tiers (prod/staging/dev)
  • ECS: scheduled scaling for business hours vs off-hours

Workflow Rules .claude/rules/workflow.md

Commands (from inspire-genius-frontend/)

  • Dev: npm run dev
  • Build: npm run build
  • Lint: npm run lint
  • Test: npm run test (watch) / npm run test:ci

Auth Service Commands (from services/auth-service/)

  • Install: pip install -r requirements.txt
  • Run locally: uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8001
  • Test: pytest tests/ -v
  • Single test: pytest tests/test_login.py -v

Deployment

  • GitLab CI on "development" branch
  • Pipeline: build → SonarQube → S3 + CloudFront

Adding a New Role-Specific Page

  • 1. Create page in src/pages/{role}/, wrap with role layout
  • 2. Add route constant to ROUTES.{ROLE} in src/constants/routes.ts
  • 3. Add route in src/routes.tsx, add nav item to NAV_ITEMS_BY_ROLE

The 6 Roles

  • user, manager, company-admin, practitioner, distributor, super-admin

Slash Commands & Session Hooks

  • Commands: /log-session, /sync-logs, /project-status, /bedtime, /doc-update
  • Hooks: .claude/settings.json fires on UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop
  • Auto-logging: .claude/hooks/update_project_log.py

Documentation

  • Update change_log.md for notable changes
  • Update database_schema.md for data model changes
  • Update CLAUDE.md for architecture changes
  • Keep .claude/rules/ current

How to Navigate the Site

  • The app has two user roles: regular user and super-admin. After login, users are routed based on their role.
  • Regular users must complete onboarding (5 tutorial screens + 2 detail forms) before accessing the main app. The ProtectedRoute component enforces this automatically.
  • The sidebar navigation is the primary way to move between pages. Each role has its own sidebar with different menu items.
  • The Alex AI floating assistant is available on all user pages (bottom-right corner) for quick AI help.
  • The ProtectedRoute component enforces authentication, role-based access checks, and onboarding completion on every protected route.

2026-08-15 — Prompt #1490 [/log-session — session rollup]
Session arc: semiprod investigation → 26pp plan → tenancy shipped end-to-end, all three PRs merged.

Merged (the individual entries below predate their merges): A.1.1 #889 → bdc83721 · A.1.3 + B.1/B.2 #903 → 9dd7966f · A.1.4 #910 → d49557cc.

The through-line: the plan's headline held — infrastructure was never the blocker. Duplicating staging-b's edge costs ~$30/mo; ~48 of the 73 engineer-days are tenancy and authorisation work no infrastructure option removes. Everything shipped this session was that work, and none of it needed a new environment.

Shipped: AuthUser.org_id in the verified token → provision_org.py seeding two client orgs on dev → ig_auth.scope consumed by dashboard, growth, document and support. Plus ~$93/month recovered by deleting an orphan Redis cache, and a latent CDK bug fixed (-c flag=false passes the string "false", which is truthy).

Decided (Bill): Option 2 — shared infrastructure, separation by key identifier. Option 3 closed.

Five of my own claims corrected mid-session, each stated before being checked: the $186 cache saving (really $93), three "broken" practitioner nav links (stale-tree artifact — the monorepo tracks 0 files under the nested frontend repo, so a diff there returns empty trivially), ig-dev-soak "draining credits" (inert), the plan's own source-of-truth assumption (FK makes org_service.* impossible), and a verification grep that returned 12 and proved nothing.

2026-08-15 — Prompt #1482 [publish Meet_the_Team.mp4 to S3]
/full-go: add this video to S3 and provide a durable url — IG Movies, Decks/Meet_the_Team.mp4.

Published: the public demo asset bucket. 12,761,538 bytes, video/mp4, H.264 1920x1080 + AAC, 6 min 41 s. Verified HTTP 200, accept-ranges: bytes, range request → 206 (scrubbing works), cache-control: public, max-age=86400.

Caught before upload: the source had its moov atom AFTER mdat (ftyp, free, mdat, moov), so a browser would have had to download all 12 MB before playback started. Remuxed with ffmpeg -c copy -movflags +faststart — stream copy, no re-encode, no quality loss; codecs and the 400.9 s duration unchanged. Confirmed on the SERVED object that bytes 32-47 are the moov header, so the fix survived the upload.

Why that mattered: the publish helper only transcodes non-web formats and uploads .mp4 as-is — publishing the original directly would have shipped the non-streaming atom order.

No ACL change: public read comes from the bucket policy, not object ACLs, so a plain s3 cp sufficed. No CloudFront in front of this bucket, so the S3 REST URL is the durable address and the key was live immediately with no invalidation.

2026-08-15 — Prompt #1488 [#908 dev rollout completed, user-sync stub incident, staging-b promoted]
Continuation of “merge 908 and deploy to dev, then tag for staging-b”.

Result: all seven #908 stacks deployed green on dev; staging-b promoted via tag release-stable-2026-08-15-cdk-asset-hash-seven-stacks, all six promote jobs green including the authenticated smoke matrix.

Incident — my #908 change shipped a stub. ig-dev-user-sync went 872 KB → 187 bytes and failed every invoke with Runtime.HandlerNotFound. The stub-zip gate failed the run, so nothing rotted silently. Repaired by mono #912: 187 B → 954,467 B, invoke now returns HTTP 200 with a live Aurora result.

Root cause — a bespoke env var nobody sets in CI. This stack’s tryBundle guard checked ONLY DISABLE_LOCAL_BUNDLE_STUB; every other bundled stack and cdk-deploy.yml itself use CDK_DOCKER_BUNDLING. All ten stacks were checked — user-sync is the sole outlier — so in CI the guard never fired and tryBundle wrote its stub. The fix accepts either spelling.

The uncomfortable part: SOURCE hashing had been HIDING this, and OUTPUT exposed it. Under SOURCE, CDK reused the previously published good asset and discarded the stub, so the broken guard stayed invisible — possibly for months. Under OUTPUT the stub earns its own hash and SHIPS. OUTPUT is still correct, but it removes an accidental safety net, so every tryBundle guard now has to actually be right. That is the inverse of the failure #906/#908 set out to fix. Impact was nil — dev is cut over so the handler is already a no-op, 24h invocations were 2 (both diagnostic), and the stack is dev-only — but the mechanism is what matters. Third stub incident for this Lambda.

Two corrections to the previous entry. (1) “staging-b was never damaged — the promote was deliberately held” is superseded: dev was proven clean first, then the promote ran and staging-b was verified against a pre-promote baseline. (2) “The tell is ZERO ‘Bundling asset’ lines” does not generalise — that grep returns zero for the per-service stacks even when bundling ran correctly, so it reads as a false positive. The reliable check is behavioural: a real FastAPI+Mangum service returns “unable to infer a handler” (module imported, app constructed); a stub raises at import.

On the tag’s scope: it necessarily carries another terminal’s #903, and that is required rather than incidental — #903 flips createSharedCache to false in the promote workflow, so tagging any earlier commit would have RECREATED the ElastiCache that terminal had just deleted. Its provision_org.py refuses --apply on staging-b, so no data mutation rode along.

Two open gaps recorded: the promote workflow has no stub-zip detector — the very gate that caught this on dev — so staging-b was verified by hand instead; and retention-stack/agent-engine-stack still keep SOURCE on dev via conditional hashing, leaving dev the same blind spot for them. Left alone deliberately.

2026-08-14 — Prompt #1481 [HomeV2 PRISM Report opens a new tab]
/full-go: on HomeV2 on Prism Data-> Prism Report(PDF). This should open in a popup window or a seperate tab.

Root cause: window.open("", "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer") returns null by spec. The handler already opened a tab synchronously inside the click gesture and redirected it once the presigned URL resolved — but with noopener (or noreferrer, which implies it) there is no handle to redirect, so it fell through to window.location.href = url and replaced Home with the PDF.

Measured, not assumed: Chrome 150, inside a real user gesture (a synthetic click is nulled by the popup blocker either way) — with those features → NULL, without them → a usable handle.

Fix: open with no features so the handle survives, then sever the opener by assignment (win.opener = null) — the same protection the flag was there for. The blocked-popup fallback no longer navigates the current tab; it raises a toast with an “Open report” action, and clicking that is itself a user gesture so opening with the URL up front is not blocked.

Why the tests were green: they mocked window.open to return a fake window, which a real browser refuses to do here — a mock cannot reproduce a null return. Tests now pin the call SHAPE and assert the opener is severed. 6 tests (was 4); both halves verified to gate.

Left alone: the other window.open call sites pass the URL directly, so a null return costs them nothing.

The sync refuses rather than loses. It will not shrink a file, will not publish audit residue, verifies the HTML tag inventory is unchanged, and archives mirror-only headings before replacing them. Open everywhere lets categories drift until the same person is filed under “Collaboration” and “Teamwork” at year-end with no way to reconcile. F1–F6 all ship in Phase 1 — with one design partner they were dodgeable, with plurality they are not, because OKR / competency matrix / quota / MBO / scorecard / values+goals need every one between them. F6 is rating passthrough, never computed.
Schema: new performance_frameworks, measure_groups, measure_approvals; measures gain framework_id, parent_measure_id, target_bands, group_key. Never cascade a framework delete. Effort 122/132 → 136/150h; Phase 0 runs the Intake against 2–3 unlike frameworks.
Also restored: Ledger_Framework_Intake_Brief.docx (14pp reusable per-framework instrument), and the generator fix — body()/bullet()/numbered()/callout() never parsed inline bold, only table() did, so bold in prose printed as literal asterisks. What it does: adds AuthUser.org_id populated on BOTH JWT paths; _extract_org_id() reading custom:organisation_id (the attribute the pool has declared since creation) plus three alternates, with blank/whitespace normalised to None; auth-service now mints org_id on all three HS256 sites; and a Cognito Pre Token Generation v2 Lambda, because access tokens carry no custom attributes without one and v1 customises only the ID token.

Found along the way: magic_link._build_session_response was already fetching organization_id and discarding it — one line from the payload the whole time.

The invariant: an absent organisation yields None and nothing else — never the sub. The bug removed is dashboard-service's org_id = user.get("org_id", user["sub"]), which always resolved to the caller's own sub: a filter that looked like tenancy and matched nothing.

Safety: OFF by default behind -c cognitoPreTokenTrigger=true; cdk diff ig-dev-cognito -c env=dev reports "There were no differences". The handler is fail-open and never raises — it sits in the login path of the whole pool, so an exception would lock out every user including whoever would roll it back. Fail open on auth, fail closed on data.

Verified: auth-service 170 passed, ig-auth 96 passed / 1 failed, Lambda 17 passed, CDK tsc clean, synth checked both flag states. The single ig-auth failure is pre-existing — it fails identically on a pristine origin/development checkout (78/1 there vs 96/1 here). Passes alone, fails in-suite: event-loop pollution, left alone.

Not deployed. Attaching a trigger to a live pool puts a new function in the login path of an environment with real testers — merging is safe on its own, but enabling deserves a watched deploy rather than an unattended one.

2026-08-12 — Prompt #1478 [401 refresh/retry loop bounded — a guard that could never trip]
A single session emitted refresh-token requests without bound — ~2.5/sec, sustained, no logout. Every refresh returned 200; the refresh was never the problem.
The guard could never trip. src/lib/axios.ts tracked retried requests in a WeakSet keyed on the axios config object. The retry is issued as instance(original), and axios mergeConfigs that into a brand new object — so the second 401 arrived as a config the set had never seen. 401 → refresh → retry → 401, unbounded.
Measured, not assumed. Against axios 1.11.0: config identity is not preserved across a retry, but a custom property does survive the merge. The marker now rides on the config. Running the new tests against the pre-fix interceptor does not merely fail — it exhausts the Node heap (FATAL ERROR: JavaScript heap out of memory), which is the loop reproduced.
Second, latent bug: refreshPromise was cleared after the await, which never runs if the refresh rejects — latching a rejected promise so every later 401 would force a logout. Now cleared in .finally().
Order mattered. The 401 originated server-side; fixing the client guard alone would have converted an infinite loop into a forced logout, which is worse. Both shipped together, and /v1/notifications joined the non-critical 401 list — a passive notification bell must never be able to end a session.
Onboarding: already disabled (ProtectedRoute, 2026-07-21); navigateAfterAuth routes every authenticated user to their role home, /home → HomeV2 workspace. Added the one missing test case — the is_onboarded flag absent, not just false.
Verification: build clean · eslint clean on touched files · 220 tests across 28 suites. FE PR #412.

2026-08-12 — Prompt #1482 [employer-specific practice interviews → question packs + build plan] /full-go
“I want to offer practice interviews with questions for roles at AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Oracle, LinkedIn, and other top technology and business consulting companies, Financial institutions (goldman sachs, citigroup, bridgewater, Black Rock), and other sector leading companies. Create a word document with a set of questions for each company, and sector and a plan to implement them in practice interview.”
Delivered docs/plans/Employer_Interview_Question_Packs.docx (18pp, render-verified) + generator scripts/build_employer_interview_packs.py: 16 employer packs, 7 sector packs, 138 questions, each with the competency it probes and what a strong answer covers, plus a 6-phase implementation plan.
Grounded, not invented. Every question maps to a real competency id in star_interview_bank.py — checked programmatically against the module (12/12 competencies used, zero unknown ids), not by eye. Each employer pack names that company’s own publicly published framework (Amazon’s Leadership Principles, Google’s four attributes, McKinsey’s PEI dimensions, Citi’s Leadership Standards, Bridgewater’s Principles …). Stated plainly in the doc: these are written in the style of those frameworks, not anyone’s real or leaked questions, and imply no endorsement.
⚠️ The discovery that shaped the plan: InterviewFrame already collects company and industry — and throws them away before tailoring. So this is two optional request fields on an existing endpoint plus a curated dataset, not a new subsystem. Design rule: curated-first, model-second, because an LLM asked what Amazon asks will confabulate confidently.
Flagged as the real constraint: Phase 0 is legal — nominative use of real employer names in a paid product, standing disclaimer, SME sign-off on 138 questions. 2026-08-12 — Prompt #1322 [401 refresh loop root-caused — notification inbox + a retry guard that never tripped]
can Kim Long and Brittany Ward login with a magic link and use the platform with no password / fix this; after Kim's password login at 22:13 the frontend fired 132 /v1/refresh-token calls in 7 minutes … Then make sure no one is sent to the onboarding process. Everyone upon magic link authorization should go directly to My Workspace. /full-go
Magic link: yes, and Kim already had. [email redacted] redeemed one end to end — POST /v1/magic-link/verify 200 + auth.user.login, nine seconds after the send. All five ECPS users are is_active, Cognito CONFIRMED + enabled, profiles complete. “Brittany Ward” is Brittany White ([email redacted]); no Ward exists. She has never requested a link — capable, untested. No password is read anywhere in the magic-link path.
The loop had two causes, both required. (1) broadcast-service GET /v1/notifications raised 401 whenever the token carried no email claim — which is the normal shape of a Cognito access token, so every password login hit it. The sibling counter route degraded to zero on the same input, giving the tell: unread-count 200 and notifications 401 for the same token in the same second. (2) The client retry guard was a WeakSet keyed on the axios config object, but the retry is instance(original) and axios mergeConfigs that into a new object — so the second 401 was never recognised.
Measured, not assumed. Against axios 1.11.0: same object across retry? false. Running the new tests on the pre-fix interceptor does not merely fail — it exhausts the Node heap (FATAL ERROR: JavaScript heap out of memory). The loop is unbounded. Backend tests fail 7-of-10 against pre-fix code.
Order mattered. Fixing the client guard alone would have converted an infinite loop into a forced logout — worse. Both shipped together, plus /v1/notifications added to the non-critical 401 list so a passive bell can never end a session.
Onboarding: already correct, one gap closed. Forced onboarding was removed on 2026-07-21 and navigateAfterAuth already routes everyone to their role home (/home → HomeV2 workspace). My initial reading came from a stale worktree on another terminal's branch and was wrong. Added the missing test case: the flag absent (magic-link / Cognito shape), not just false.
Also corrected: the Magic-Auth AccessDenied is scoped to /v1/magic-auth and falls back to the SECRET_KEY env var; /v1/magic-link/* never reads that secret. It never blocked magic-link login — the earlier hold on removing ECPS passwords rested on a wrong premise.

Root cause. PRISM returns no direct-download PDF URL: the completed-history SubActionURL1 is an auth-flow token or the literal string "User not found" (confirmed live on staging-b for Kevin and [user M.T.]). So the ingestor's _download_pdf failed and stored a 136-byte header-only placeholder — a %PDF header with no page tree, which every viewer reports as "failed to open." The only real URL PRISM hands back (UnlockReport.action_url_1) is an HTML candidate-portal page, not PDF bytes. Scores were never affected (FetchReportData/EntityTypeID, #854). Distinct from site-orphaning (#851).
Fix (#872). The ingestor now renders the downloadable PDF from the committed scores via the same compose_self_portrait → build_prism_report_payload → docgen path the in-app "View Inventory PDF" button uses, so the stored file and on-screen read can't disagree. New _looks_like_real_pdf guard + async _generate_report_pdf; PDF resolution moved after the scores commit; placeholder written only if rendering itself raises.
Verified. 41 PRISM tests pass; agent-engine suite (4985 tests) collects clean. Live in the staging-b runtime Kevin renders to a real 17,399-byte %PDF-1.7 (Red 95 dom / Gold 91 / Green 31.5 / Blue 30.5, 8 dims) — working PDF delivered to the operator. Merged to development (squash dc676b2b); dev staged-deploy rolls the agent-engine. staging-b promote pending; the two stored placeholders self-heal on re-ingest post-promote (a direct S3 overwrite is blocked by the auto-mode classifier).

The framing correction first: Claude Code’s permission system is a guardrail against model error, not a sandbox against a person — an interactive session can generally reach a shell. This repo’s own deny Bash(python3 -c *) beside allow Bash(python3:*) is the illustration: it stops a casual inline snippet, not a human who writes a .py file. Third-party addresses in tracked files: 108 private, 67 in the PUBLIC frontend repo — confirmed live on its origin/development, including a paying customer’s institutional address. public/IG_project_log.html is in the Vite public/ dir, so it is very likely served on the deployed site too. migration_mapping*.csv carry name + email + Cognito ID + role + PRISM flags per person. what roles have access to self-portrait, moments, goals, job fit? / provide users access to self-portrait, moments, goals, and job fit. Gate these as well /full-go (both tiers, entitlement across all six roles)
Role was never the gate. All four surfaces sit under /vertical/*, which ProtectedRoute does not role-check — it only enforces roles on the five role-prefixed path groups. Access is a per-user row in public.user_entitlements, and that table has no role column. What was actually blocking each one: Self-Portrait and Moments had no entitlement holders outside ~9 super-admins; Goals was unlocked for [email redacted] alone; Job Fit was in FORCE_DISABLED_VERTICALS, greyed even for entitled users.
The gate was never enforced. require_vertical had existed since the vertical model landed and was applied to zero routes. Entitlement decided what the UI offered; the API served any authenticated caller. Greyed buttons were standing in for an authorization boundary.
Both halves, in order. Entitlements seeded FIRST (115 users on dev, 114 on staging-b, all six roles, merge semantics — 0 pre-existing keys lost, diffed against a user_entitlements_bak_20260811 snapshot), THEN the gate. Reversed, the gate 403s exactly the super-admins reaching these surfaces through the *_dev_access preview override.
Gate design: vertical_router(key, entitled=True) attaches the dependency at the ROUTER level, so a route added later is gated by construction rather than by the author remembering. /health moved to a new VerticalManifest.public_router — it answers “is this vertical wired?”, not “what does this user have?”. blueprint-service serves /v1/blueprint/fit/* itself, so it got its own check on the same table; fails CLOSED on a DB error.
Deliberately not gated: /v1/agents/goals (shared Summit store — growth-service's TDS dossier reads it for managers with no direction-setting entitlement) and /v1/agents/blueprint/{explain-fit,write-resume} (LLM formatters over fit data the caller already holds; the data surface feeding them is now gated).
A test that failed open. The first blueprint route test walked app.routes, passed locally and found ZERO routes in CI on identical fastapi/starlette — verified by rebuilding a venv from the service's pinned requirements. I could not reproduce it, so rather than guess I rewrote it to read app.openapi()["paths"] and assert non-empty first: the original form treated “no ungated routes” and “the walk stopped working” as the same result.

2026-08-07 — Prompt #1319 [Agent-engine test backlog cleared + CI gates armed — MERGED, dev + staging-b]
restore Goals / what needs to be done to complete goals discovery based on prisom and additional information scores? / fix the 174 failing tests on development what is this? / fix the aiosqlite loop scoping and re-land the gate / promote the backend to staging-b
The gates were fake. agent-engine ran 180 failed / 4527 passed on development and nobody could see it: backend-ci.yml appended || true to pytest, and pr-validation.yml narrowed agent-engine to three files. Two green ticks per PR, nothing verified. Now 4810 passed in CI with both gates enforcing.
117 of 180 were ONE fixture. ProviderFactory._providers is CLASS state and conftest registered the mock once at import; any test calling reset() without restoring it emptied the registry for everything after. Later agents got Available: [], fell into their error path and returned the apology at confidence 0.3. Whole files looked broken yet passed in isolation.
Three production bugs found via the tests: Meridian's keyword classifier tokenised with lower.split(), so any keyword followed by punctuation was invisible (“growth,” matched nothing while “help” matched business — misrouting coaching messages); _resolve_canonical_sub ran an UNBOUNDED DB query inside require_auth on every authenticated request; and the WS loop never handled websocket.disconnect, so every disconnect exited through the error handler.
The CI hang — three stacked causes. pytest-asyncio pinned ^0.25 while local venvs had drifted to 1.x, so CI ran 0.25.3 and deadlocked against the StaticPool sqlite connection; :memory: forces that shared connection and starlette TestClient runs on its own loop; plus the WS bug. I called it “Linux-only” — wrong, it reproduces on macOS with 0.25.3. Lesson: reproduce CI from the PINNED deps before trusting a local pass.
Rejected / skipped honestly: session-scoped loop scope (breaks two tests relying on per-test isolation); two org_id tests skipped as Postgres-only (CAST(:org_id AS uuid) is numeric on SQLite) rather than relaxed. backend-ci stays masked for the OTHER services — unaudited, trainer-service has ~97 known failures.
Shipped: PRs #825 (5dc9d50f) + #838 (74668857); promoted release-stable-2026-08-07-test-backlog-and-gates. ECS-exec verified on dev AND staging-b; health 200 / auth 401 / CORS 204 on both.

“The tiles you created are very long, shorten them but display their info. In Moments don’t display the full history list — it should be displayed when selected in the dropdown.”
The tiles shipped hours earlier were taller than the rows they replaced. Seven columns inside a 1280px container is ~169px per tile, and at that width every sentence wrapped to four or five lines — tiling had defeated its own purpose. The face now carries only number, state icon, name and chips; question and outcome moved into the tile title with the full readiness sentence.
Readiness stayed visible as a coloured chip (Ready / Thin: PRISM) — it is the difference between a door you can open now and one that will disappoint you. Only its wording shrank: new NEEDS_SHORT for the chip, NEEDS_LABEL kept for the tooltip.
Measured, not eyeballed: jsdom has no layout engine, so the 4452-test suite is structurally incapable of catching tile height — the exact thing being changed. Rendered the real component against the real built CSS and measured: tile 192px → 78px, grid 392px → 164px, unchanged 169px width, 13 tiles in two rows of 7+6.
Moments no longer prints the whole history on load. Nothing renders until a Moment is picked; “All Moments” survives as a choice rather than the default. The picker now shows from the first Moment (gating on two would strand a single-Moment user with guidance they cannot open), and a selection that vanishes from a refetched feed falls back to unpicked rather than to the whole list. The none-picked state says “You have N Moments on file” — never “no Moments”.
Tests strengthened, not relaxed: readiness now asserted on the chip and the tooltip, so shortening the face cannot quietly drop detail; Moments cases select before asserting — several would otherwise have passed because nothing renders at all.
One deploy check was badly designed and proved nothing — grepping the deployed chunk for the long readiness sentence hits either way, since that string is now the tooltip text. The evidence for shortening is the measurement.

Seven columns inside a 1280px container is ~169px per tile, and at that width every sentence wrapped to four or five lines — tiling had defeated its own purpose. The face now carries only number, state icon, name and chips; question and outcome moved into the tile title with the full readiness sentence.
Readiness stayed visible as a coloured chip (Ready / Thin: PRISM) — it is the difference between a door you can open now and one that will disappoint you. Only its wording shrank: new NEEDS_SHORT for the chip, NEEDS_LABEL kept for the tooltip.
