Rendered the real component against the real built CSS and measured: tile 192px → 78px, grid 392px → 164px, unchanged 169px width, 13 tiles in two rows of 7+6.
Moments no longer prints the whole history on load. Nothing renders until a Moment is picked; “All Moments” survives as a choice rather than the default. The picker now shows from the first Moment (gating on two would strand a single-Moment user with guidance they cannot open), and a selection that vanishes from a refetched feed falls back to unpicked rather than to the whole list. The none-picked state says “You have N Moments on file” — never “no Moments”.
Tests strengthened, not relaxed: readiness now asserted on the chip and the tooltip, so shortening the face cannot quietly drop detail; Moments cases select before asserting — several would otherwise have passed because nothing renders at all.
One deploy check was badly designed and proved nothing — grepping the deployed chunk for the long readiness sentence hits either way, since that string is now the tooltip text. The evidence for shortening is the measurement.

/full-go — “create business and implementation plan to capture weekly performance data for an employee … capture what the employee is measured on as individual metrics … on a daily basis capture by voice what progress the employee made … produce weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual summaries … at year end a factual bulleted list of metrics mapped to measurements, with a narrative that can be added to the evaluation tool used by the company.”
Delivered: docs/plans/Performance_Ledger_Business_and_Implementation_Plan.md plus the generated 49-page .docx (scripts/build_performance_ledger_plan.py). Business case (problem, buyer, packaging, competitive position, risks) and implementation plan (domain model, daily loop, mapping, rollups, year-end export, architecture decisions, schema, API, frontend, voice, privacy, phasing, tests, infra, metrics).
Premise verified first, not assumed. Both repos were on foreign branches, so everything was read from origin/development. The gap is real: measure_id, performance_metric, success_criteria and attainment all return zero hits across every Python service and the frontend. The scorecard/evidence hits are Job Blueprint, the STAR interview scorer, the College Scorecard API and Honor grounding — none is employment performance measurement.
Most of the machinery already exists. app/memory/rollups.py + routes/rollups.py + services/wave-b-rollup-trigger/handler.py already run weekly/monthly/quarterly rollups on an EventBridge cron; app/voice/* is the full STT/TTS/turn-detection stack; chronicle_agent.py + bio_capture.py are the guided-interview→structured-record pattern; app/scoring/star_scorer.py is the zero-model-call evidence scorer; growth-service owns manager↔member authz and already reads the Summit goal store server-side. The plan assembles these rather than rebuilding.
Key decisions: store in the Agent Engine (app/performance/, migration 029 — head was 028, re-confirm) not a 26th service; Meridian routes to a new Coaching specialist Ledger; the employee confirms every evidence→measure mapping, enforced in schema, SQL and API; deterministic aggregation with generated narration (the model never computes a number that reaches an appraisal); reuse the existing rollup cron; text-first then voice; export contract not HRIS connectors; PERFORMANCE_LEDGER_ENABLED as an allowlist (absent → 404).
Two things deliberately withheld. No third-party workforce statistics are cited — the usual appraisal-cost figures are on the do-not-cite list, so the value case is argued structurally with a note that primary sources are needed before any customer-facing deck. And a daily self-reported performance log is discoverable in an employment dispute and a works-council matter in several jurisdictions — flagged as a legal/commercial decision to take before Phase 1.
Render-verified (49pp → PDF → PNG → read). One layout defect found and fixed: the table-cell renderer only honoured a leading **bold** marker, so mid-string bold rendered literally. Replaced with a general inline parser. Effort estimate: ~122 human hours + ~132 Claude Code hours, 9 phases, ≈9–11 calendar weeks. No service or frontend code changed.

2026-08-08 — Prompt #1314 [PRISM report orphaning: make visible + prevent (site-pinned fetches) + backlog remediation]
Root-caused why some PRISM reports silently never appeared and shipped the fix (PR #851, merged to development, deploying to dev). MECHANISM: after the live-creds go-live the process-wide PRISM client was repointed to the live SiteID, but candidates created on the OLD staging SiteID were still fetched with the CURRENT client — so FetchCandidateHistory/FetchReportData silently queried the wrong site, returned IsAuthorised=false with empty data, and the ingestor persisted a hollow 'done'. CODE (agent-engine): (1) client `_ensure_authorised()` raises PrismClientError on IsAuthorised=false for FetchReportData (NOT EI — supplementary add-on legitimately unauthorised for non-EI candidates), so the ingestor marks the row failed with the PRISM reason + report.ingest_failed event; (2) new `get_prism_client_for_site(site_id)` resolves the client from the row's stored site_id (current/empty → singleton; other site w/ creds in the secret's optional `sites` map → cached pinned client; other site w/o creds → fail-fast PrismClientError naming both sites) — poller resolves per-row, ingestor standalone path per-site; (3) create_request refresh path now repoints site_id/client_id/reference alongside the link. +7 tests, 544 PRISM tests pass; no migration/CDK/flag. OPS (staging-b): confirmed a stranded candidate's report loads properly after a User-Management CSV import (mirrors to prism_results — verified 4 quadrants + 8 behaviours populated), flipped that user's onboarding flags, closed the stale request row; re-created two other stranded candidates on the live site (fresh questionnaire links) with tracking rows repointed to live — one whose original qtype (42) is unsupported on the live SiteID was re-issued on the standard qtype (4). Verified new users are created on the live site now (both dev + staging-b), so the orphaning is a closed one-time cutover, not an ongoing leak. Also generated a staging-b account-status .docx for a separate user check.

2026-08-07 — Prompt #1469 [Agent-engine test backlog cleared + CI gates armed — MERGED, dev + staging-b]
restore Goals / what needs to be done to complete goals discovery based on prisom and additional information scores? / fix the 174 failing tests on development what is this? / fix the aiosqlite loop scoping and re-land the gate / promote the backend to staging-b
The gates were fake. agent-engine ran 180 failed / 4527 passed on development and nobody could see it: backend-ci.yml appended || true to pytest, and pr-validation.yml narrowed agent-engine to three files. Two green ticks per PR, nothing verified. Now 4810 passed in CI with both gates enforcing.
117 of 180 were ONE fixture. ProviderFactory._providers is CLASS state and conftest registered the mock once at import; any test calling reset() without restoring it emptied the registry for everything after. Later agents got Available: [], fell into their error path and returned the apology at confidence 0.3. Whole files looked broken yet passed in isolation.
Three production bugs found via the tests: Meridian's keyword classifier tokenised with lower.split(), so any keyword followed by punctuation was invisible (“growth,” matched nothing while “help” matched business — misrouting coaching messages); _resolve_canonical_sub ran an UNBOUNDED DB query inside require_auth on every authenticated request; and the WS loop never handled websocket.disconnect, so every disconnect exited through the error handler.
The CI hang — three stacked causes. pytest-asyncio pinned ^0.25 while local venvs had drifted to 1.x, so CI ran 0.25.3 and deadlocked against the StaticPool sqlite connection; :memory: forces that shared connection and starlette TestClient runs on its own loop; plus the WS bug. I called it “Linux-only” — wrong, it reproduces on macOS with 0.25.3. Lesson: reproduce CI from the PINNED deps before trusting a local pass.
Rejected / skipped honestly: session-scoped loop scope (breaks two tests relying on per-test isolation); two org_id tests skipped as Postgres-only (CAST(:org_id AS uuid) is numeric on SQLite) rather than relaxed. backend-ci stays masked for the OTHER services — unaudited, trainer-service has ~97 known failures.
Shipped: PRs #825 (5dc9d50f) + #838 (74668857); promoted release-stable-2026-08-07-test-backlog-and-gates. ECS-exec verified on dev AND staging-b; health 200 / auth 401 / CORS 204 on both.

2026-08-06 — Prompt #1463 [Lumen: one nav row + Moments in Meridian history]
Three changes. (1) Removed the Lumen second button row — "Back to Inspire Genius" plus an "or switch to" list of every other entitled vertical — and moved Back to Inspire Genius up into the tools row, pushed to the end since it is the one control that LEAVES Lumen. Nothing unreachable: the sidebar Tools section lists the verticals on every page; the switcher only duplicated it. (2) Removed "Coaching" from the Lumen nav — checked FIRST that the Lumen Dashboard still links to it, so the page is not orphaned; it lives in LUMEN_TOOLS which feeds BOTH the pill row and the sidebar by design, so one deletion covers both. (3) BACKEND: a Moment now appears in Chat with Meridian history. The key finding is that the conversation list is DERIVED, not stored — GET /v1/chat/conversations groups chat_messages by session_id and titles it from the first user row — so there is no conversations table and writing two messages IS creating the conversation. The situation becomes the History title (what a person scans for), the guidance is the assistant row attributed to Meridian, keyed moment-<id> so a retry cannot double-write. NEVER fails the ask (the Moment is already in the feed; a mirror failure logs and returns), writes nothing on an empty body rather than a title with no reply, and covers PULL Moments only — proactive scheduler Moments are excluded because the user never asked anything and History should record what they said. ALSO ADDED LumenNav tests, which did not exist — that is why deleting a whole switcher broke nothing; the new tests mock entitlements GENEROUSLY so a reinstated switcher fails loudly instead of passing against an empty fixture. FE 552 suites / 4411 tests; BE tests/lumen 33 passed and the full agent-engine suite's 174 failures were confirmed IDENTICAL to the untouched baseline (AWS-credential tests) by re-running on a stash. VERIFIED DEPLOYED: dev ECS taskdef :56 COMPLETED and ECS-exec found the new function twice in the running container; the stable LumenNav chunk has zero hits for "or switch to"/"Coaching"/listEntitledVerticals and LUMEN_TOOLS is exactly Dashboard/Self-Portrait/Moments. NOT DONE: the backend is dev-only — staging-b needs a separate release tag promote, a deliberate stop.

2026-08-05 — Prompt #1457 [ts-jest emit failure blocking deploys — diagnosed and fixed]
A test suite had been failing to COMPILE on GitHub runners — never an assertion failure; every occurrence read "4363 tests passed, 1 suite failed to run" with ts-jest's "Unable to process <file>, make sure outDir is neither '' or '.'". Four times across unrelated branches, and on #370 it went DETERMINISTIC: three consecutive reruns of the same commit all failed, skipping both deploy jobs and leaving the HomeV2 rework undeployable for over an hour. Cause read from ts-jest 29.4's source, not inferred: the throw at ts-compiler.js:193 is reachable ONLY on the LanguageService path, guarded at :74 by `isolatedModules`; setting it in tsconfig.test.json switches to per-file transpileModule, which cannot reach the throw. COSTS NO TYPE SAFETY — jest.config.ts already sets diagnostics.warnOnly:true, so jest was paying for a type-aware program and deriving nothing from it; real checking is `npm run build` (tsc) as its own CI job, and tsconfig.test.json is test-only so the build is untouched. RESULT: Unit Tests 25 min -> 2m47s on the same runner, and green. THE MISTAKE THAT MADE THIS TAKE FOUR ROUNDS: `npm run test:ci` is bare `jest` with NO --coverage, while CI runs `npx jest --ci --forceExit --coverage --coverageThreshold=...` — so every "550/550 green" reported earlier never exercised the failing path, while being described as the identical CI command. Re-verified with the real invocation. Also corrected mid-task: my first proposed fix put the flag in the ts-jest transform options, which is deprecated in 29.x and only sets a TypeScript flag rather than selecting the transpile path. Deployed and verified on stable: bundle hash moved, welcomeBackPrefix/otherAssessments/MeridianEngageCard gone, Moments chunk reachable from HomeV2, and all 6 new i18n keys SERVED (checked en/es/ja/ar/tr on both tiers — runtime-fetched, so repo presence is not evidence).

Seven Home-page changes on request: removed the Chat-with-Meridian tile (WelcomeBackTile moves up into its place, so "move the 2nd tile to the top" falls out of the removal); removed "Other Assessments" plus its now-unreachable Add-assessment modal and the loaded-frameworks read whose only consumer it was (still addable from Documents — the shortcut went, not the capability); replaced "Welcome back, {name}" with "Here's what you worked on last visit" + recent Meridian conversations and relative times, from the SAME query the chat History dropdown uses so the two cannot disagree; added the videos line beside the Videos control and corrected the spelling to InspiresGenius; greyed+locked Self-Portrait and My Journey via a per-SHORTCUT lever (LOCKED_QUICK_ACTIONS) kept deliberately separate from the vertical-level force-disable, because Lumen and Direction Setting are still live products; moved Personal Info to the end of the quick-action row, sized to content, panel floating (an inline expansion inside a flex row shoves the layout on every open); and added a "Today's Prep" tile embedding Lumen Moments via a new `embedded` VARIANT rather than a copy, so tile and page cannot drift. PROCESS NOTE: `gh pr merge --auto` fell back to an IMMEDIATE merge (auto-merge not enabled on the repo), so #370 landed on three of four green gates with Unit Tests still pending — no practical consequence, but --auto is not a safe gate here.

2026-08-05 — Prompt #1458 [ts-jest emit failure blocking deploys — diagnosed and fixed]
A test suite had been failing to COMPILE on GitHub runners — never an assertion failure; every occurrence read "4363 tests passed, 1 suite failed to run" with ts-jest's "Unable to process <file>, make sure outDir is neither '' or '.'". Four times across unrelated branches, and on #370 it went DETERMINISTIC: three consecutive reruns of the same commit all failed, skipping both deploy jobs and leaving the HomeV2 rework undeployable for over an hour. Cause read from ts-jest 29.4's source, not inferred: the throw at ts-compiler.js:193 is reachable ONLY on the LanguageService path, guarded at :74 by `isolatedModules`; setting it in tsconfig.test.json switches to per-file transpileModule, which cannot reach the throw. COSTS NO TYPE SAFETY — jest.config.ts already sets diagnostics.warnOnly:true, so jest was paying for a type-aware program and deriving nothing from it; real checking is `npm run build` (tsc) as its own CI job, and tsconfig.test.json is test-only so the build is untouched. RESULT: Unit Tests 25 min -> 2m47s on the same runner, and green. THE MISTAKE THAT MADE THIS TAKE FOUR ROUNDS: `npm run test:ci` is bare `jest` with NO --coverage, while CI runs `npx jest --ci --forceExit --coverage --coverageThreshold=...` — so every "550/550 green" reported earlier never exercised the failing path, while being described as the identical CI command. Re-verified with the real invocation. Also corrected mid-task: my first proposed fix put the flag in the ts-jest transform options, which is deprecated in 29.x and only sets a TypeScript flag rather than selecting the transpile path. Deployed and verified on stable: bundle hash moved, welcomeBackPrefix/otherAssessments/MeridianEngageCard gone, Moments chunk reachable from HomeV2, and all 6 new i18n keys SERVED (checked en/es/ja/ar/tr on both tiers — runtime-fetched, so repo presence is not evidence).

2026-08-03 EDT — Prompt #1443 [Re-import the outstanding PRISM CSV — proved impossible, corrected my own earlier claim]
Asked to re-import the one outstanding user’s PRISM CSV so her scores load. It cannot work — and the reason disproves something I had written twice. THE CLAIM I CORRECTED: both the #794 changelog and the TODO said “fix = re-import her CSV”. I fetched her actual file from S3 (a single copy, byte-identical across dev and staging-b) and ran the production parse_prism_csv on it: it reproduces exactly the rows already stored, which is precisely why they carry score_type = NULL. Her original import was faithful; the source export is incomplete — one populated score row with an empty variant label holding only 26 of 89 values, with the other two variant rows entirely blank, against a well-formed export’s three labelled rows. RULED OUT THE TEMPTING SHORTCUT: “it is row 0, so it must be Underlying.” I surveyed all 13 well-formed exports rather than assume — 10 lead with Adapted, only 3 with Underlying. Position carries no information, so the inference was unavailable. WHY I STOPPED RATHER THAN JUST LOADING IT: her 8 quadrant behaviours are present and numeric, so derive_colours would run and her profile would appear immediately — the single blocker is not knowing whether those numbers are Underlying, Adapted or Consistent. Since prism_results is read as the authoritative profile platform-wide (chat injection, dashboard, Job Fit), loading an unknown variant would quietly present a real person’s adapted behaviour as her natural style. That is a correctness risk, not pedantry, so I put the choice to Bill with the trade-off stated instead of picking. Decision: obtain a fresh complete export from the PRISM portal; loading the existing row as Underlying was explicitly rejected. No code and no data changed, and the downloaded copies of her personal CSV were deleted afterwards. She remains the only outstanding case on either environment.

2026-08-03 — Prompt #1441 [Summit interview: built, undriven — W7]
How will the goal setting process work? It should be a directed interview session that drives to the why of the goal.
It is exactly that, it is built, and the frontend does not call it. Five discovery categories behind three live routes: POST /ask/{category} (warm intro + contextual questions, PRISM-anchored, stance is "exploration, not interrogation"), POST /why-ladder (asks why for 3–5 rungs, stops at "a value, identity, or emotional root", hard-capped at 5 so it cannot badger), and POST /synthesize (answers + PRISM → structured goals carrying motivation = the WHY-ladder root, prism_alignment, a quadrant-keyed execution_style, success_metric, and a reward-framed first_step).
Verified live: /why-ladder returned "What draws you toward operations — what do you picture yourself doing once you're in that role?" — a real probe, not a stub.
But nothing drives it. goals.service.ts exposes only getGoalSession, patchGoal, deleteGoal. The FE calls none of the three interview routes; SummitDiscovery only displays category status. 2026-08-03 EDT — Prompt #1432 [/full-go — PRISM dual-store fix + backfill (#794)]
Investigated whether [user G.B.]’s PRISM scores were in the staging-b DB, and the answer turned into a platform bug: imports were landing in a table nothing reads. THE FINDING: `assessments`/`assessment_scores` is the canonical assessment store, but a repo-wide grep showed no runtime code reads it — `routes/prism.py`, `memory/long_term.py`, `rag/prism_vectorizer.py` and dashboard-service all read `prism_results`. [user G.B.] and [user B.B.] each had a complete, authoritative 107-row import that the application could not see: nothing in chat, on the dashboard or in RAG, and `latest-prism` 404ing — while the data looked perfectly healthy in SQL. I had to correct my own framing mid-thread: I first reported the impact as just a missing HomeV2 checkmark and a 404. Reading the consumers proved it far broader — the scores were invisible to the whole runtime. ALSO CORRECTED A PREMISE IN THE REQUEST: fixing the writer alone would not have fixed [user G.B.] and [user B.B.] (code only affects future uploads) and [user D.R.] needed nothing at all (she already had a `prism_results` row and loaded fine) — so this was two pieces of work, not one, and I said so before starting. THE FIX: `_project_to_prism_results()` mirrors PRISM assessments into `prism_results`, deriving colours with `prism_canon.derive_colours` — the same function the app reads through rather than a second SQL copy of the quadrant pairing, which has been rotated once already. Wired into all three admin write paths, not just the CSV import the prompt named: `reprocess` regenerates scores, so leaving it out would strand stale colours. Idempotent via `uuid5` + `ON CONFLICT` because `prism_results` has no unique key on `user_id`. Incomplete dimension sets write nothing — a half-populated radar chart is worse than an absent one. INCIDENTAL DRIFT FOUND: `prism_results.created_at`/`updated_at` existed in Postgres (added by `r29_...sql`) but never in the ORM model, so SQLite tests silently diverged from production — the same class of drift that previously shipped a 500. BACKFILL: staging-b 27→29 rows; [user G.B.] and [user B.B.] now resolve. Confirmed the written colours exactly match what the read-path self-heal recomputes. One user deliberately left alone: [user Am.C.]’s legacy import has `score_type = NULL` and one unidentified variant of 3 — 17 of 18 other legacy imports label all three, so hers is broken, not a convention, and guessing the variant would invent data. The backfill reports users it cannot fix instead of silently omitting them. VERIFICATION: 3 new tests proven non-vacuous by reverting the source fix; full suite 4425 passed with the same 171 pre-existing failures as origin/development (sets diffed, zero introduced); 31/31 PR checks green; and the deployed code confirmed inside the running dev container via ECS exec rather than trusting “deploy succeeded”. Stated plainly as NOT done: staging-b’s agent-engine still runs the old code (backend promotion is tag-gated), so a future upload there would recreate the problem — though the staging-b data itself is repaired.

2026-08-03 EDT — Prompt #1443 [Re-import the outstanding PRISM CSV — proved impossible, corrected my own earlier claim]
Asked to re-import the one outstanding user’s PRISM CSV so her scores load. It cannot work — and the reason disproves something I had written twice. THE CLAIM I CORRECTED: both the #794 changelog and the TODO said “fix = re-import her CSV”. I fetched her actual file from S3 (a single copy, byte-identical across dev and staging-b) and ran the production parse_prism_csv on it: it reproduces exactly the rows already stored, which is precisely why they carry score_type = NULL. Her original import was faithful; the source export is incomplete — one populated score row with an empty variant label holding only 26 of 89 values, with the other two variant rows entirely blank, against a well-formed export’s three labelled rows. RULED OUT THE TEMPTING SHORTCUT: “it is row 0, so it must be Underlying.” I surveyed all 13 well-formed exports rather than assume — 10 lead with Adapted, only 3 with Underlying. Position carries no information, so the inference was unavailable. WHY I STOPPED RATHER THAN JUST LOADING IT: her 8 quadrant behaviours are present and numeric, so derive_colours would run and her profile would appear immediately — the single blocker is not knowing whether those numbers are Underlying, Adapted or Consistent. Since prism_results is read as the authoritative profile platform-wide (chat injection, dashboard, Job Fit), loading an unknown variant would quietly present a real person’s adapted behaviour as her natural style. That is a correctness risk, not pedantry, so I put the choice to the product owner with the trade-off stated instead of picking. Decision: obtain a fresh complete export from the PRISM portal; loading the existing row as Underlying was explicitly rejected. No code and no data changed, and the downloaded copies of her personal CSV were deleted afterwards. She remains the only outstanding case on either environment.

2026-08-03 — Prompt #1299 [Assessment import — ranked reports 422’d; 3 faults fixed]
HomeV2 changes + “the upload of other assessments is failing fix it”
Root cause: _normalize required every parsed row to carry a number or a text label, treating anything else as noise. A ranked instrument has neither — a Clifton Strengths report ranks themes with no numeric score and no label — so every row was discarded, scores came back empty, and the endpoint raised 422 “No scores or typing could be parsed”. Rank is now a real result.
Two related faults fixed: _coerce_number was a bare float(), which rejects "85%", "72 / 100" and "1,234" — and a failed coercion then caused the whole row to be dropped as noise. And max_tokens=4096 truncated long ranked reports mid-JSON, surfacing as an opaque “invalid extraction”; raised to 8192.
The diagnosability gap that hid it: the empty-result path logged nothing — CloudWatch showed the Anthropic call returning 200 OK then a bare 422. It now logs the response shape (keys, row counts) and never the content, since these are users’ personal assessment reports.
How it was found: /ecs/ig-staging-b-agent-engine showed two POST .../import/preview → 422, each preceded by Extracted 25851 characters from PDF (19 pages) and a successful Anthropic call — so extraction and the model both worked and the fault had to be in normalization. Dev showed only OPTIONS preflights and no real calls (no traffic), so CORS was checked and cleared first.

2026-08-02 EDT — Prompt #1298 [magic-auth gate denylist + staging-b auth verification path]
Corrected a standing mischaracterisation, then found a real defect behind it. staging-B's POST /v1/magic-auth → 404 had been carried as a bug “blocking live authenticated verification” and was queued to be fixed. It is not a bug: magic-auth mints a valid HS256 session token from an email address alone — no password, no emailed link, no one-time-use — and PR #717 deliberately gated it off the non-dev tiers. “Fixing” the 404 would have re-opened an authentication bypass on a shared environment. The gate was re-verified in the deployed config (MAGIC_AUTH_ENABLED=false on ig-staging-b-auth-service) and by 22 passing auth-service tests. The real defect: the gate was written as a denylist — (isProd || envName === 'staging-b') ? 'false' : 'true' — which names the environments to protect. config.ts defines four (dev, staging, prod, staging-b), so staging matched neither arm and resolved to 'true': the bypass would have deployed enabled there. Never exploited — staging has never been deployed, only ig-dev-auth-service and ig-staging-b-auth-service exist — but it shipped open by default. Now an allowlist (envName === 'dev' ? 'true' : 'false') so an unrecognised env fails closed. This is the fourth instance of the envName === '...' shape (after #738, #745 and the API-Gateway throttle bug); the first three were performance bugs, this one was an auth bypass. No deploy needed — for both deployed envs the synthesised value is unchanged (dev 'true', staging-B 'false'); only the undeployed staging changes. Pinned: test/magic-auth-gate.test.ts, 6 assertions across all four envs plus a set-equality check so a future env added to the permitted side fails CI — and it was confirmed red against the old expression before being committed (2 failures naming staging exactly). Built the path the 404 was being blamed for: scripts/stagingb_verify/ — verify_auth.py asserts the 404 still holds, logs in through the ordinary /v1/login Cognito path, hits /v1/me, and with --chat runs a live Meridian turn asserting PRISM behaviour. Preconditions verified first: pool MFA OFF, ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH on, no client secret — so password login needs no mailbox. Blocked, by design: provision_account.py creates the synthetic account and sets its password; both were refused without explicit owner approval and are left pending rather than worked around. Two traps documented: /v1/magic-link/request always returns 200 (anti-enumeration), so it is not an existence check; and every identity in the staging-B Cognito pool is a real person (wilkescc.edu / robeson.edu students, PRISM staff, Honor Foundation), so verification uses a synthetic account rather than impersonating one.
2026-08-02 EDT — Prompt #1297 [/log-session — full session wrap]
One thread, five merged PRs, three staging-b promotes — all from "how many concurrent users can the architecture support?" The answer was a code defect, not an infrastructure limit, and each fix exposed the next one. (1) #736 — the provider built a sync Anthropic client and called it inside async def, freezing the worker's event loop for the whole ~20s call and capping an ECS task at two concurrent turns regardless of task count. Async client: measured 1/250 → 250/250 in-flight, and loop-ticks 0 → 18 (a heartbeat coroutine that previously never got scheduled at all — the production symptom). (2) #736 — removing that ceiling made CPU autoscaling blind, since a worker holding network waits burns no CPU; replaced with a PeakInFlightLLMCalls signal, an ALB backstop and a saturation alarm, keeping CPU/memory as safety nets. Two design points came from measuring, not reading: the instantaneous gauge misses bursts (7 concurrent read as a 1-minute average of 0.167), and the publisher is a worker, not a task. (3) #737 — CI itself was pinning dev's autoscaling floor to 0 after every merge, via a hardcoded restore whose justifying comments had been false since July; CloudTrail showed 10 consecutive lift/restore pairs. Verified fixed across three consecutive rolls, with zero scalable-target writes. (4) #745 — nothing ever set AGENT_ENGINE_ENVIRONMENT, so staging-b published Environment=dev while its policy watched Environment=staging-b: an inert policy that reported healthy. (5) #753 — 429s became a signal rather than a generic error (LLMRateLimited, emitted even at zero so it can be alarmed on, plus a retry-budget dial left at its current value deliberately). Zero regressions throughout — 167 suite failures before and after, byte-identical set, checked by diffing the failure set rather than the count, because the suite is already red on development. Three of my own claims were wrong and were corrected in place: "deployed CDK is stale" (it wasn't — CI was the cause), "the staging-b account doesn't exist" (it does — magic-auth is deliberately gated off and returns a different string for that case), and "no retry/backoff on 429s" (the SDK always had it; visibility was what was missing). 2026-08-01 EDT — Prompt #1283 [prism colour fix + TTS dedupe + injection latency]
PRISM colour scores, the phantom “Orange”, duplicated TTS read-back, and slow prompt injection — five reported defects. (1) Red was being called “Orange”. PRISM has four colours — Gold, Green, Blue, Red. “Orange” survives only as the legacy prism_results.orange DB column name, and it leaked into the model's context two ways: the injected profile block emitted <orange>, and Aura's prompt said verbatim “Treat Red and Orange as synonyms; mirror the user's wording.” The model was doing what it was told. Block now emits <red>; Aura's and Meridian's prompts forbid the word; six reference/knowledge modules no longer offer it as an alias; and a narrowly-scoped output guard rewrites it only in PRISM contexts so “orange juice” survives. (2) The Blue score was wrong — and so were Gold and Red. Each colour is the mean of its quadrant's two behaviours, but the pairing was rotated against the licensed manual. Proven against dev assessment 4f1066ba: Blue read 78.0 where Supporting 92 + Coordinating 80 gives 86.0; Gold held Red's pair and Red held Blue's. Only Green was correct — its pair is identical under both groupings, which is why the error survived. The row's own raw_data.color_derivation recorded the wrong pairing in plain text. The rotation lived in four places and was documented in-code as “a pre-existing, deliberately-unfixed quadrant-mapping inconsistency”; all now derive from one source of truth (app/prism_canon.py). Bill reported Blue; three of four colours were affected. No data migration — colours are derived at READ time from the authoritative assessment_scores rows, so all 10 dev users corrected instantly; legacy rows self-heal from raw_data.dimensions. No UPDATE was run against user data. (3) “Scores get misrepresented at times.” Not staleness — the read is already per-turn and uncached. The hazard was absence: memory sections render in priority order and each is gated on remaining token budget, so enough corrections/goals silently pushed the entire <prism_profile> block out of context, leaving the model to answer from numbers seen earlier in the conversation. Its cost is now reserved up front. (4) Meridian read answers back twice. speakText had no re-entrancy protection — it replaced the abort controller without aborting the previous one, so the first run's in-flight sentences kept resolving into an audio queue that is a plain FIFO with no dedupe. Two clean runs read the whole answer twice; two overlapping runs interleave and repeat fragments — both reported symptoms, one bug. Now deduped on content, with a genuine abort. Verified non-vacuous: removing the guard makes the test fail with both sentences synthesized twice, in order. (5) Injected questions were slow and showed scaffolding. The warm-up health ping and the auto-send fired in the same tick, so an injected question got zero warm-up window and hit a cold ECS task — paying API GW's 30s cap plus retry backoff. A typed question never pays this because the typing time IS the warm-up window; that is the entire gap. Dispatch now waits for the ping (capped at 8s), bubbles still render immediately. Plus prefillDisplay so Lumen's composed “sources in scope” prompt reaches the model while the bubble shows only what the person asked. 2026-08-01 EDT — Prompt #1284 [prism colour guard — negation fix]
PRISM colour guard: don't rewrite “Orange” when the model is saying it isn't a colour. Follow-up to the same-day PRISM fix. Found by an adversarial probe against deployed dev, not by a test. Asked “Am I an Orange? What does my Orange score mean?” — the case most likely to defeat the fix — Meridian correctly replied “Your quadrant is called Red in PRISM — there is no Orange colour in the framework.” The normalise_colour_names output guard then rewrote that second “Orange” (it was followed by “colour”, one of the quadrant-noun contexts) and what actually reached the user was “…there is no Red colour in the framework” — self-contradicting nonsense, in precisely the situation the guard exists to serve. Everything else in that probe was correct: Red 34 (Focusing 7 / Delivering 61), Blue 92, Green 91.5, Gold 52 — all matching the corrected derivation — and “Orange” appeared nowhere else despite the user using it four times. Standing lesson: any regex that rewrites LLM output will eventually corrupt a correct sentence; probe the adversarial case, and remember the prompts + injected profile block are the real fix — the rewriter is only drift insurance. 2026-08-01 EDT — Prompt #1285 [prism brain map + score-type comparison]
PRISM Brain Map diagram, plus a read-only Underlying-vs-Consistent score-type comparison for every dev user. (1) The Brain Map. The four colour scores were only ever prose; they now arrive as the canonical map with labels and scores. The layout is not a free choice — it comes from the licensed reference text (AXES_DISCERNING_DYNAMIC): Gold top-left, Green top-right, Red bottom-left, Blue bottom-right. Two things a naive 2×2 gets wrong, both encoded and asserted against the rendered SVG geometry so nobody can quietly rotate it the way the score pairing was: the axes are DIAGONALS (Gold+Blue = Discerning, Green+Red = Dynamic), and opposites mirror HORIZONTALLY rather than through the centre, so Evaluating faces Initiating and Focusing faces Supporting. Delivered in metadata["prism_map"], never in the response text — TTS speaks content, and an inline SVG there would be read aloud as markup (the exact failure mode removed earlier the same day); a markdown table and one-line description carry the identical numbers for TTS, screen readers and plain-text export. When it fires: deliberately NOT every PRISM turn — a map on “what does high Focusing mean?” is clutter. Primary signal is that the answer actually quotes ≥2 of the user's four colour scores (self-correcting, no keyword list to maintain), with an explicit “show me my profile” as a second trigger; number matching is boundary-guarded so 52 doesn't match 1952. A bug this nearly shipped with: the first cut read context.metadata["prism_scores"], as several existing call sites do — that key is never populated on the REST or WS chat paths, so the map would have silently never rendered. Scores now come from the memory manager behind a cheap no-DB pre-check. Frontend: rendered via a data-URI <img>, not dangerouslySetInnerHTML — an <img> cannot execute script under any circumstance; encodeURIComponent not btoa (the map contains ↔ and ·); alt is the full numeric read-out so screen readers get data, not “image”. buildTurnHtml gained an optional figure field rather than smuggling markup through the escaped markdown body, with a test asserting the body is still escaped. Render-verified: the SVG was rasterised and looked at — the first version put the axis captions on top of the panel borders, illegible and invisible in the source. (2) Underlying vs Consistent — reported, nothing changed. PRISM measures each behaviour three times (Underlying = instinctive, Adapted, Consistent = the manual's “likely overall behaviour”). The platform derives every colour from Underlying only. Across all 14 dev users: 52 of 56 colour scores would change under Consistent, mean shift 8.5 points, max 22.0, 25 intensity-band changes, almost entirely downward. The consequence that matters: many scores drop out of the ≥75 overdone-strength band that drives specific coaching language — user 3468e498 reads Green 91.5 / Blue 92 (both flagged overdone) under Underlying versus 74 / 72.5 under Consistent, so those warnings would vanish. Nothing was changed — switching would silently move every number for every user; that's a product decision for Bill or a PRISM practitioner. Incidental: six dev users share byte-identical scores (78/50.5/86/39) — almost certainly duplicated test data. Also learned: the migration-runner Lambda truncates result sets at 10 rows; earlier queries looked complete but were silently cut off — aggregate into a single json_agg row for anything larger. Verified: agent-engine +31 tests, 4305 passed, failure set byte-identical to origin/development (zero regressions); FE +12 tests, 529 suites / 4171 tests, exit 0 under CI's exact coverage gate; build clean. The actual reason is that POST /v1/magic-auth is deliberately disabled on staging-b because it hands out a valid session from an email alone, and when disabled it returns "Not found" to hide the endpoint. 2026-08-01 EDT — Prompt #1288 [close 735 and fix the MinCapacity drift]
Closed #735 as superseded by #736 — then found my own root-cause claim was wrong. I had reported the dev MinCapacity: 0 vs config.ts staticMin: 1 mismatch as "the deployed CDK is stale relative to config". First thing this session was to check that, and the deployed CFN template actually says MinCapacity: 1 — the infrastructure was fine. Something outside CloudFormation was writing 0. Ruled out scheduled actions (describe-scheduled-actions → zero) and the /agent-stop skill, then CloudTrail gave it up: 10 consecutive deploys since 2026-07-27, each a min=1 lift followed ~3 minutes later by a min=0 restore, every one from gha-agent-engine-roll-*. The culprit is CI. The roll-ecs-dev job in agent-engine-image.yml lifts the floor to 1 for the deploy window and restores it to a hardcoded 0; since that job is the last writer and CloudFormation only reasserts MinCapacity on a stack update, every merge to development left dev unable to recover from a scale-to-zero — which is exactly why dev chat sat at 503 the night before. The step's own comments justified the 0 with two claims that stopped being true on 2026-07-19 when dev went always-on: "off-hours scheduled scaling sets min=0" and "schedule cron will reassert its own min on next firing". There is no cron left to reassert anything. 2026-08-01 EDT — Prompt #1287 [fix the CPU autoscaling next]
The follow-up the async fix created: ECS could no longer tell when it was saturated. CPU target-tracking at 70% only ever worked because the Anthropic client was synchronous — a blocked worker pinned a thread, so load surfaced as CPU. After PR #735 a task can hold hundreds of concurrent in-flight LLM calls at near-zero CPU, so the service would saturate silently: turn latency climbing and jobs queueing behind the DB pool while the autoscaler saw an idle fleet. Fix: the app now publishes what actually correlates with load (app/observability/saturation.py — an in-flight gauge wrapped around provider.chat()/stream(), with the stream counted for the whole generator lifetime, plus a lifespan-managed reporter), and CDK gains a primary target-tracking policy on that metric, an ALBRequestCountPerTarget backstop for the poll storm the gauge can't see, and a saturation alarm — because target tracking goes quiet once it's already pinned at maxCapacity. CPU/memory policies were kept as safety nets rather than ripped out; they still catch genuine compute pressure. Two design points came from measuring on dev, not from reading code, and both invalidated the obvious implementation: (1) the instantaneous gauge systematically misses bursts — a real burst of 7 concurrent calls registered as a 1-minute average of 0.167 because every 30s sample landed between ~11s waves, so the policy now tracks the per-interval peak; (2) the publisher is a worker, not a task — uvicorn runs --workers 2 and each worker reports (SampleCount 4/min for one task), so the target is calibrated per worker (dev 10 ⇒ ~20 turns per task). Verified live: sustained 15-concurrent load (~7.5/worker) read 7.75; idle read 0.0 every tick so scale-in isn't starved; a transient 30-turn burst read 7.5 avg / 16 max and correctly did not cross the target — a 21s spike that ends before a task can boot shouldn't earn permanent capacity. Not verified, and said so: an actual scale-out event — the policy doesn't exist in AWS until a CDK deploy, which was deliberately not run locally (local deploys re-bundle and can clobber the stack's Lambdas). Full-app cdk synth is blocked locally by the trainer-stack ig-auth pip/cffi bundling, so verification went through a focused Template.fromStack(AgentEngineStack) test — the repo's first real CDK test (the existing one was a commented-out stub) — 7 assertions incl. pinning the dimension set, since adding a per-task dimension would split each publisher into its own stream and silently break the per-publisher Average that target tracking's capacity math depends on. Tracing the constraint chain from the CDK config landed on a code-level defect, not an infrastructure one: AnthropicDirectProvider built a sync anthropic.Anthropic client and called messages.create() / messages.stream() inline inside async def chat / async def stream. THEN EXPLAINED THE DEAD WEBSOCKET PUSH. _run_chat_job pushes a job_complete frame so a connected client renders immediately instead of waiting for the next poll, and the frontend has the matching notifyPushFrame short-circuit — but it has never fired once. push_to_user() resolves recipients from self._user_sessions, an in-memory dict of native FastAPI sockets held by that ECS task; in production the browser's socket terminates at API Gateway → ws-proxy Lambda, never at the task, so the dict is always empty and the call returns 0. It fails silently by construction: the call site logs on success and at DEBUG on exception, but delivered == 0 is neither, so the failure path emits nothing at all — which is why it went unnoticed. Confirmed four independent ways: zero hits for "pushed completion" over 3 days of staging-b logs; no execute-api:ManageConnections on the ECS task role (granted only to the ws-proxy Lambda); APIGW_WS_ENDPOINT absent from the entire CDK; and the correct LambdaConnectionManager exists but is scoped by its own docstring to "the Lambda deployment path". Consequence: delivery is entirely the 2s poll, costing 0–2s per turn and far more in a backgrounded tab where Chrome throttles setInterval to ~1/min — likely part of why 60s was felt while the logs showed 49s. This corrected my own earlier claim in the same session that the completion fetch was push-triggered; that had been inferred from a poll landing 67ms after an LLM call, which was coincidence. ANSWERED THE FOLLOW-UP by checking the call sites rather than reasoning from memory: fixing it will NOT add latency — both pushes run after the terminal update_status, i.e. after the answer is already fetchable, so they sit off the user-visible path; the fix adds ~10–50ms to a background task and subtracts the 0–2s poll wait. Recorded the implementation caveat that matters: keep the push after the status write and best-effort, because moving it earlier or making it blocking would put an external API call on the critical path.

Lumen coaching answers on the page, with print + Word/PDF export. Personal coaching now answers inline instead of navigating away to the Meridian chat surface — asking used to throw the person out of Lumen and discard the context they had just assembled with the source checkboxes, so the answer arrived somewhere that no longer knew why it had been asked. Answers accumulate (a run of questions reads as one session) and each one can be copied, printed, or exported to Word or PDF — the same per-turn controls Meridian chat has. How: the ordinary async-job path (POST /v1/agents/chat/async → poll GET /v1/agents/chat/jobs/{id}). Meridian is not bypassed — she still classifies and routes to whichever specialist the question needs. No backend change, so no promote is needed: Job Fit could answer inline (#306) because it already had explain-fit; Lumen has no equivalent, and a synchronous LLM route would sit behind API Gateway's hard 30s cap. The poll is the delivery mechanism (the job_complete WS push is not reachable through the production ws-proxy), so the hook opens no socket at all. Decisions worth keeping: print and export share one document builder, so the printout, the .doc and the PDF are the same artefact rather than three near-misses (a test pins the printed input deep-equal to the exported one); the scope line (“Draw on my PRISM scores…”) is an instruction to the coach, not part of the question, so it goes into the prompt but is kept out of the answer heading and the exported file — which leads with the question, because a download read a week later has none of the on-screen context; printTurn uses an off-screen iframe rather than window.open, which a popup blocker swallows silently leaving no error to explain the nothing that happened; one job at a time, and a start-job failure clears the pending state since onJobSettled never fires for a job that was never accepted. Verified against dev before merging, not asserted: real token, chat/async → 202, poll → running → complete in ~9s, and contributing_agents came back ['Summit'] — Meridian routed a goal question to the goal agent, the routing this design depends on. Tests: 97 passing across pages/lumen/, hooks/lumen/ and lib/exportTranscript/; three existing tests asserted the old navigate-away behaviour and were rewritten to express the new intent rather than deleted. Stayed off SelfPortrait.tsx / types/lumen.ts — FE #312 was open on those from another terminal and merged mid-build; re-checked after, no conflict. Known duplication: #312 landed lib/lumen/portraitReport.ts at almost the same time. It shares the plumbing (renderHtmlToPdf, downloadBlob) but has its own HTML builder and markdown converter, because a portrait report is a genuinely different document shape from a single turn; this work reuses buildTurnHtml because a coaching answer is a turn. Duplication limited to two small markdown converters — accepted for now rather than fixed by refactoring another terminal's freshly-merged code; extract on the third occurrence or the first behavioural drift. FE #313; frontend-only, so it reaches dev and staging-B on merge.

2026-07-29 EDT — Prompt #1385 [LOE: Meridian Projects tile persistence — estimate only]
LOE assessment for the Meridian “Projects” tile — estimate only, nothing shipped. Bill asked for the human + CC cost of giving the tile a real backend (today it is a localStorage-only list, so projects do not follow a user across devices or survive a cache clear). The estimate turns on one finding, and I measured rather than guessed: there is no conversations table — GET /v1/agents/conversations derives the list with GROUP BY session_id over chat_messages, and a conversation’s title is a sentinel row (__CONV_TITLE__:) inside the message stream. So there is nothing for a project_id to hang off, which separates “persist the list” from “projects that group chats” by roughly an order of magnitude. Scope A (parity, persist the list): CC 2–3 · Human 2–3 h · confidence A — anchored to a near-exact measured analogue, Lumen saved-prompts (BE 073cef07 = 669 insertions/6 files; FE 97599c2 = 417 insertions/8 files; the two commits landed 8m36s apart inside the 4h42m block that produced 5 BE + 5 FE PRs). Projects is simpler — no use-count promotion. Scope B1 (group conversations via a session_id join table): CC 4–6 · Human 5–8 h · confidence B — the join table is not the risk; every list query needs a project filter, which means editing the GROUP BY query with its hand-written correlated subqueries and its “search mode loads up to 10,000 rows” fallback, the most load-bearing query in the chat surface. Scope B2 (promote conversations to a first-class table): CC 10–15 · Human 12–20 h · confidence C — no comparable in the repo, ±100% until spiked; a refactor of chat persistence, not a feature. Scope C (delete the tile): CC <1 · Human 0.25 h — ~95 lines of frontend. Two overheads priced in that are easy to forget: a new backend test file will not run in any gating job unless added to the hardcoded 13-name allowlist at pr-validation.yml:222, and the FE coverage gate is a global 55% with ~5 points of headroom. Also re-confirmed the local monorepo checkout is 383 commits behind origin/development, so every figure was read from the remote, not the working tree. Recommendation: do not build Scope A — persisting the list makes the feature look real while the control still does nothing; take Scope C now, or B1 when grouped chats are actually asked for.

2026-07-29 EDT — Prompt #1383 [500 on requesting a PRISM assessment — /full-go, multiple concurrent types]
Bill pasted a console dump: “Failed to request PRISM assessment: Request failed with status code 500” plus CSP / unload / kwift.CHROME.js noise. Separated signal from noise first — the CSP and permissions-policy lines are browser-extension chatter, unrelated to the app; the only real event was the 500. THE LOG READ THAT CHANGED THE DIAGNOSIS: CloudWatch showed httpx: POST …/api.svc/CreateCandidate "HTTP/1.1 200 OK" immediately before the failure — PRISM UK had already created the candidate; our own INSERT then blew up with UniqueViolationError on uq_prism_requests_user_external_ident. So this was never a PRISM outage. The live questionnaire URL was sitting in the failed INSERT’s bound parameters, so it was recovered from the log and handed to Bill immediately — he could take the survey while the fix was built. ROOT CAUSE: the constraint was UNIQUE (user_id, external_ident) and the route always sets external_ident = str(user_id), so it collapsed to ONE PRISM REQUEST PER USER, FOR LIFE — a second questionnaire was impossible, not even a different TYPE (Bill picked QTypeID 1 / Professional while holding an earlier row). The 24h idempotency guard did not save it because it only matches rows with completed_at IS NULL, so a completed or stale row fell straight through into a doomed insert. And the ordering made it expensive rather than merely annoying: PRISM is called BEFORE the insert, so every attempt minted a real candidate, burned a licence seat, and threw the link away with a 500. SAID PLAINLY THAT THIS WAS NOT A REGRESSION from the FE work — it was unreachable until the frontend started submitting, which is exactly why prism_requests had 0 rows in both environments. The FE fix exposed a pre-existing backend defect. FIX (BE #720) after Bill chose “multiple concurrent types”: constraint → UNIQUE (user_id, external_ident, qtype_id) (migration 023 + migration-runner mirror); idempotency pre-check scoped per qtype_id so an in-flight Foundation request stops suppressing a Professional one; INSERT wrapped in except IntegrityError to refresh the existing row onto the newly-issued link rather than 500 — once PRISM has created the candidate a DB conflict must never reach the user. Re-requesting the SAME type stays guarded by the 24h window, i.e. policy in the route rather than in a constraint that can only fail after the third-party call. CHECKED THE POLLER BEFORE WIDENING THE KEY (it select()s a list and loops per row, so multiple rows per external_ident are safe) rather than assuming. THE CATCH I FOUND BY TRACING MY OWN FALLBACK: against an UNMIGRATED database the legacy key fires for a different qtype, the handler finds no same-qtype row to refresh, and re-raises — so merging the code alone would NOT have fixed Bill’s case. Migration first, then code; stated explicitly instead of letting it be assumed. Added ERROR-level logging of the issued ActionURLs on that unpersistable path — the same mechanism that rescued tonight’s link, turning a burnt seat into a recoverable incident. VERIFIED against a measured baseline rather than a bare number: full agent-engine suite 167 failed / 3821 passed vs baseline 167 failed / 3818 passed — identical failure count, +3 from the new tests, with the 167 confirmed pre-existing by re-running the suite with the change stashed. Both changed test files sit in pr-validation.yml’s agent-engine allowlist, so they genuinely gate rather than silently passing. 2026-07-28 EDT — Prompt #1380 [staging-b: /prism-assessment cannot request a PRISM report from PRISM UK — investigate, then /full-go the fix]
Bill, testing on staging-b: "I am on stagingB testing the /prism-assessment request a prism report from prism UK. Please investigate why this isn't working?" ROOT CAUSE: the submit button was a no-op — it never fired a network request at all. PrismInitiateForm was built as a design-time harness whose real API call lives behind an optional onSubmit prop; both PrismAssessment.tsx:96 and PrismAssessmentV2.tsx:103 render it as <PrismInitiateForm disabled={...} /> with no onSubmit, so the handler terminated at onSubmitProp?.(values, apiPayload) against undefined. Zod validated, a payload object was built, and it was silently discarded — no request, no toast, no error, no visible change, which is exactly the "nothing happens" symptom and the hardest kind to diagnose from the UI. PROVED IT AGAINST THE DEPLOYED BUNDLE, NOT JUST SOURCE, because the local FE checkout was on a stale feature branch and the live page showed a "Check existing customer" control that branch did not have: pulled the live chunks and found the page chunks passing a single prop (I,{disabled:!!n} and the V2 variant A,{disabled:!!m}), the minified handler ending at j?.(s,a), and the harness tell-tale staging.prismbrainmapping.com/questionnaire/demo shipped in production. SECOND HALF OF THE DEFECT — the form was written against a route family that was never built. Probing staging-b directly: POST /v1/prism/initiate 404, /history/{userId} 404, /status/{id} 404, /report/{id} 404; only POST /v1/prism/requests (401 — exists, auth-gated), /requests/me, /check-customer and /poll/run are live. Cause of the split: prism_request.py mounts at /v1/prism while prism.py mounts at /v1/agents/prism — a different prefix — and prism.service.ts targets the former path with the latter's assumptions. So even a one-line prop fix would have 404'd. THE WORKING PATH ALREADY EXISTED and was pointed out as the interim workaround: RequestPrismDialog → useRequestPrismSurvey → POST /v1/prism/requests, reachable from the Home "Take PRISM Assessment" tile and the chat PrismBadge. FIX (FE PR #300): the form now calls useRequestPrismSurvey() itself, mapping questionnaireTypeId→qtype_id, languageId→lang_id, gender==='male'→gender (PRISM convention: true = male) and isGift (backend aliases is_gift). showPayloadPreview becomes the explicit harness switch so /dev/prism-test-harness keeps its preview-only, no-network behaviour, and onSubmit is demoted from a replacement for the API call to an observer fired alongside it — the prop shape that caused the bug is the prop shape that no longer can. ONE NON-OBVIOUS CALL: the success screen was gated on questionnaireUrl being truthy, so a request that succeeded but returned no action_url_1 would have fallen straight through to the form and reproduced the very "nothing happens" symptom being fixed — re-gated on an explicit submitted flag with a fallback message. SCOPED OUT DELIBERATELY and said so: Assessment History and Import Existing Report on that page stay inert — usePrismHistory is already knowingly disabled (enabled: false, backlog #10.U) because its endpoint was never built, so it is not a live 404 and repointing it at /v1/prism/requests/me is a separate change; reference and createUser stay form-only as CreateRequestBody has no matching fields. VERIFIED: 5 new wiring tests (payload mapping, link render, no-link fallback, failure path, harness-mode-stays-offline), 11/11 on the file; full suite 502 suites / 3817 tests pass with no regressions; npm run build clean; ESLint clean on all 3 changed files. Then re-ran the same bundle check that proved the defect against the rebuilt output: the form chunk now imports usePrismRequest-*.js (which carries /v1/prism/requests) and the submit path compiles to await b.mutateAsync({forename...}) — neither present before. Work done in an isolated worktree so Bill's checked-out branches were untouched; PR body kept free of infra identifiers since the FE repo is public.
2026-07-28 EDT — Prompt #1379 [/full-go — move Job Fit + Lumen into My Workspace]
Job Fit and Lumen moved out of the collapsed “Verticals” launcher and into My Workspace (FE PR #298). The reasoning behind the placement, not just the placement: both are first-person surfaces — the signed-in user working on their OWN profile — so they belong next to Goal Setting and My Documents as everyday tools, rather than reading as separate products you launch into. GRANT, Knowledge Continuity and Honor stay where they are, because they genuinely are separate workspaces with their own sub-nav. Implemented against the registry rather than hardcoded per layout: a WORKSPACE_VERTICALS set is filtered out of useVerticalLauncherSection and re-surfaced by a new useWorkspaceVerticalItems, so the two lists can never disagree and nothing is double-listed — adding a third workspace vertical later is a one-line set edit. They also get real icons (Briefcase/Lightbulb) instead of the launcher’s generic Compass, which would have been indistinguishable once inside a menu of distinct icons. Three details that were decisions, not defaults: the items splice in above the Settings/Help tail rather than appending, because Settings and Help being last is a convention users navigate by muscle memory; the merge falls back to append for menus with no such tail (practitioner’s ends at Analytics); and it returns the same array reference when there is nothing to merge, so a user entitled to neither vertical does not get a new array identity on every render feeding the navSections memo in every layout. Covered every chrome, not just the one I was looking at — UserLayout and SuperAdminLayout build their menu directly from getUserNavItems(), while manager/company-admin/practitioner/distributor come through useGatedNavItems → UnifiedLayout; a fix in one would have silently missed four roles. Entitlement gating deliberately untouched: the gate is still enabled_verticals through Vertical Core, so a user without the entitlement sees no new item. Verified: 502 suites / 3812 tests pass, npm run build clean, 0 new lint errors on the 9 touched files (the one error reported is a pre-existing props: any in a test mock). Nine new tests exercise the splice against the real registry rather than a mock — position, tail-less append, stable identity, route de-dupe, and the launcher exclusion that prevents double-listing.
2026-07-28 EDT — Prompt #1378 [implementation plan with LOE (man, CC) using the multi-subagent approach]
Bill: "build a implementation plan with LOE (man, CC) using the multi-subagent approach." Read as two parallel cost columns — human engineer-hours vs Claude Code sessions — planned around parallel subagent execution lanes. DELIVERED IG_Direction_Setting_Implementation_Plan.docx (17 pages) + generator scripts/build_direction_setting_implementation_plan.py: 51 work items across 7 phases + cross-cutting, each with owner lane, dependency, confidence grade and both cost columns. Full scope 72 CC / 51 human hours; recommended launch scope (Phase 6 deferred) ~65 CC / ~49 human hours, of which ~30 human hours are NOT delegable. CALIBRATED AGAINST MEASURED HISTORY RATHER THAN INVENTED MULTIPLIERS — mined git log + change_log.md across four comparable deliveries before estimating anything. THE ANCHOR FACT: Lumen was estimated at 5–6 weeks in its own plan doc and delivered live-on-dev in ~40 hours (first commit 24 Jul 17:44 → live dev 26 Jul 09:23; the five BE + five FE PRs authored in one 4h42m block) — an estimate/actual ratio of about 20x on wall-clock. IG's past estimates have been directionally right on CC-session count and wrong on calendar by an order of magnitude, so the doc reports both and marks the calendar figures as its least trustworthy numbers. SECOND CALIBRATION FINDING: the dominant cost driver is NOT lines of code but whether a new CDK stack is needed — Lumen (rode agent-engine) and growth-service (own 447-line stack) are within 1.5x on lines and 8x apart on elapsed days, and all six growth-service post-merge PRs were infrastructure realities rather than features. That retroactively validates the build plan's "no new microservice" call as worth roughly a week of calendar. Also measured and recorded for reuse: route module 180–470 LOC (median 276 across 43 modules); backend tests 34–47% of insertions in the same commit; FE page+service+hook triad 7–9 files/+400–500; FE vertical shell 9 files/+167; one migration 2 files/~120–200 L; post-merge hardening 2–6 PRs per delivery; and ≥92% of monorepo commits carrying a Claude co-author trailer (473 of 516 non-merge on origin/development). THE HEADLINE THE DATA FORCED: agent capacity is not the constraint — human review time is. The critical path is not technical but 0.1 role list (2h) → 0.2 draft (agent) → 0.3 REVIEW 30 BLUEPRINTS (14h) → publish → matches surface → demo, and fourteen hours of one qualified person's judgement cannot be shortened by adding agents. Every compression lever in the doc therefore targets the human column, the largest being cutting the launch blueprint library from 30 roles to 15 (~7h off the critical path). Second independent path: the O*NET licence question (3h, external) blocks all of Lane D and is flagged to raise on day one despite Phase 4 being scheduled later. THE MULTI-SUBAGENT MODEL AND ITS MAIN STRUCTURAL INSIGHT: five lanes touching disjoint parts of the tree (A backend orchestration, B frontend in the separate repo, C blueprint library, D market adapter, E cheap wins) — but all five would otherwise edit the SAME SIX registration files (app/main.py, app/verticals/bootstrap.py, src/routes.tsx, src/constants/routes.ts, src/verticals/index.ts, src/verticals/core/types.ts), which are the known merge-conflict hotspots, and because CI concurrency is serialized (cancel-in-progress: false, one staged-deploy chain globally) a conflict costs a QUEUE SLOT not just a rebase. Fix: land one scaffold PR serially before any lane starts, then lanes append only. CI/DEPLOY OVERHEAD MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because on small items it dominates: the FE coverage gate is global 55% functions/lines/statements injected as a workflow env var and NOT in jest.config.ts (which has no coverageThreshold key at all), with only ~5 points of headroom and two prior threshold reductions on record where the failure landed on whoever merged second; npx tsc --noEmit checks ZERO files so only npm run build reproduces the type gate; there is no ESLint job in CI at all; backend tests DO NOT GATE — pr-validation.yml runs a hardcoded 13-filename allowlist for agent-engine and everything else sits behind || true which also neutralises --cov-fail-under=60, so adding a new test filename to the allowlist became its own work item; migrations are fully manual on both environments and staging-B promotion is ~15–20 min with 14 gating smoke routes, migrations first. ESTIMATE HONESTY stated in the doc: no completion date, no productivity multiplier (the two columns are never converted into each other), confidence graded A/B/C with the C items — ROI engine, market adapter, role-play machine — flagged as having nothing comparable in the repo and needing a spike before being trusted at ±100%; plus three named false economies including "do not skip tests because backend tests do not gate", which is a measured fact about the workflow, not a licence. VERIFIED rather than assumed: rendered to PDF, rasterised all 17 pages and measured BOTH ink coverage and margin-bleed per page, which caught four defects a clean script exit did not — column widths silently ignored (python-docx cell widths are advisory; the prose column collapsed into a tall narrow one, fixed with fixed tblLayout + explicit tblGrid); then tables running off the LEFT MARGIN because add_table() already emits a tblGrid and inserting a second left both, with the renderer picking the stale auto-sized one (fixed by replacing rather than inserting, plus normalising every width list to the usable text width so overflow is now structurally impossible); Lane E rendering gold-on-gold and unreadable; and two stale "57 CC sessions" references against a corrected total of 72. Phase totals re-checked by hand against the item rows.

Bill: "the student journey deck is not understandable. It's audience is university and community college leadership. Students and their parents. It must deliver a message of the steps of the journey and the benefits along the way to all involved. The deck needs to be 10 slides or less and be compelling with a call to action." He was right — the first deck was written in the register of the internal journey map (stage codes S0–S14, route paths, service names, status labels, a defect list, an engineering backlog). None of that means anything to a college president and less to a parent. REBUILT IG_Student_Journey_Deck.pptx from scratch: 10 slides, plain language, one ask. Structure: title → why now (three sourced numbers) → the five steps and what each gives back → steps 1–2 "being known before being advised" → steps 3–4 "the money question, answered in order" (federal aid → scholarships → real net price → offers compared → loan reality → one plan) → step 5 "where most advising stops, and why this doesn't" → what each of the three audiences gets (student / family / institution, side by side) → why this is not a chatbot → how a pilot works → the ask ("give us one cohort and one term"). Generator rewritten on the same ig_brand design system with ig_brand._footer rebound so slides carry "Inspires Genius, Inc. · Raleigh, NC" instead of the internal "· Confidential" mark — wrong to stamp on a deck handed to a president or a parent. CITATION WORK, and this is the part worth recording: the obvious hook for this audience is "students don't get enough counselling", and checking the verified stat list before writing showed that would INVERT THE SOURCE — ASCA 2024–25 has high schools broadly MEETING the recommended ratio (~205–243:1). Leading with high-school counsellor scarcity would have misstated the data to an audience that knows it. The deck runs the honest version instead: 372:1 national average against a recommended 250:1, shortfall concentrated in K-8 at 613–787:1, so students arrive UNDER-EXPLORED, NOT UNDER-SERVED — which is both accurate and a stronger argument for higher-ed leadership. Also: student debt labelled $1.86T total (federal $1.7T + private) not the misused federal-only figure; WEF 39% argued from magnitude not trend (the series decelerates, so an urgency framing inverts it); no "bias-free" claim anywhere — the difference slide states outright that no algorithm removes human judgement or bias from a life decision. NO OUTCOME PERCENTAGES ANYWHERE: no validated IG outcome numbers exist, so rather than borrow the category's invented ones the CTA *is* the measurement — one cohort, one term, a written read-out on the institution's own students, stated on the slide as "we would rather produce one real number with you than quote five borrowed ones at you." VERIFIED: rendered to PDF, rasterised, eyeballed all 10 slides; caught and fixed one collision (five-step slide footnote overlapping the page footer, row pitch tightened 0.9→0.82in), re-rendered clean. FLAGGED TO BILL: the rewrite replaced the internal-audience deck in place and its generator with it — the content survives in docs/plans/IG_New_User_Journey_Maps.md §3, but the internal slide version no longer exists as a file and would need rebuilding if wanted.

Three bugs the tests caught: pydantic's Field(min_length=) short-circuits before field_validator, so the "describe the issue in detail" guidance was being replaced by a generic "String should have at least 30 characters" — the constraint had to be dropped so the helpful message survives; the FastAPI 422 shape is {detail:[{msg}]} not {message}, so the frontend toast needed an extractor or users saw a generic failure instead of the guidance; and logging.basicConfig() is a silent no-op on Lambda (the runtime installs a root handler at WARNING before import), which swallowed every INFO record — without force=True the SES MessageId was unverifiable, so I could not have proven the email sent. Deploy trap avoided: cdk diff on ig-dev-services showed 9 unrelated Lambdas (Auth, Coach, Org, UserMgmt, Dashboard, Document, 3× Observability) with new code hashes purely from re-bundling unpinned deps — a full cdk deploy would have shipped fastapi 0.140 / boto3 1.43.56 / sqlalchemy 2.0.51 across all of them, so the support Lambda was deployed surgically and the CDK change committed for consistency. Verified on dev, not assumed: migration 002 applied via ig-dev-migration-runner (and a scare where the new columns "vanished" turned out to be the runner truncating output at rows[:10]); short description → 422 with the guidance text; full request → 201 with the contact block echoed and user_id resolved from the token; SES MessageId 0100019fa19db38a-… logged for the send to contact@inspiresgenius.com. Test tickets deleted afterwards. 78 backend tests, 25 frontend tests, clean build, 0 new lint errors. Not on staging-b.

2026-07-25 EDT — Prompt #1368 [open GAP 1 doc; build + open the "Why we go deeper on goals" document (onboarding GAP 2)]
Bill: "open IG_Why_This_Isnt_ChatGPT.doc, build the 'Why we go deeper on goals' document then open it." Opened GAP 1, then built and opened GAP 2 — IG_Why_We_Go_Deeper_On_Goals.docx (9 sections / 19 tables) via scripts/build_why_deeper_goals_doc.py. This is the Goals-Light → full-Summit bridge asset, companion to GAP 1 with the same structure and the same evidence discipline. The framing problem is different from GAP 1's and I called it out in §1: by the time this argument is made the user has ALREADY done Goals-Light and feels finished — a feeling we deliberately engineered, because the alternative was asking a stranger for a multi-session commitment before they had any reason to give it. So the job isn't "convince someone to start goal-setting", it's "convince someone who thinks they've done it that there's a materially different thing behind the door". Crucially the doc never disparages the user's Goals-Light goals (they wrote them three minutes ago; disparaging the goals disparages the user) — it's precise and generous about exactly what three minutes can and can't produce. Category line: a list tells you what you want; a plan tells you why it matters, what will break it, and what to do on Monday. §2 gives approved copy for FOUR surfaces — the "Go deeper" card (with the load-bearing "a few conversations, not one long sitting", which must never be cut because an unstated time cost is always assumed to be the worst case), Meridian's in-conversation pitch, the per-goal "deepen this one" action (flagged as the highest-converting door in — ten minutes on ONE goal they already care about — and worth building even if the others slip), and the five-category coverage strip showing career_history honestly untouched after Goals-Light, since that visible gap is the best organic prompt to go deeper and costs nothing because it's simply true. §3 runs the WHY ladder to its root TWICE: example 1 is Summit's own verbatim example ("better leadership skills" → "I refuse to be the reason someone dreads their job" — rung one is a training request, the root is an identity commitment), and example 2 is the stronger one because the ladder doesn't refine the goal, it REPLACES it ("I want to move into management" → "I want to be recognised as senior, which isn't the same as wanting to manage people") — catching someone about to spend two years pursuing a role they don't want for a recognition they could get another way. No three-minute intake catches that; the stated goal is entirely plausible and would sail through unexamined. §4 is the four-quadrant grid — "become confident presenting to senior leadership" planned four ways for Green/Blue/Red/Gold with the shape, the reason, AND what would break each, where two of the four are direct opposites; the explicit landing is that every one of those plans is good advice and three are wrong for any given person, and guessing which is what generic goal-setting does. Plus a Goals-Light-vs-Summit field table (motivation / prism_alignment / execution shape / success metric / first step / owner / status) showing what the extra time actually buys. §5 is the 75s script — shorter than GAP 1 because the audience is warmer and needs one idea — opening on the user's own kind of goal card ("This is a real goal. It's also not the real goal."), the ladder building rung-by-rung with real beats, a silent hold on the root, the quadrant grid as the SINGLE demo beat, a spread-out calendar answering the unspoken time objection, closing on "You've already told me what you want" so the CTA credits their prior work instead of implying a restart; with an explicit cut-order (never cut or speed up the ladder; never cut the quadrant beat). §6 lists 7 phrasings never to use incl. "complete your goal-setting" (frames coaching as an unfinished task and invites rushing, the one behaviour that ruins it) and "it only takes 30 minutes" (a promise you break in session two), plus 5 real objections incl. It caught a real pre-existing bug: GRANT writes never persisted — the write routes didn't commit() (get_db doesn't auto-commit by codebase convention; the data layer only flush()es when a session is injected), so every GRANT save via the API — including the existing self-serve PATCH /students/{id}/aid-intake — returned 200 but rolled back on session close (why profiles weren't saving after go-live). Also built the two requested enhancements: co-access toggle (invite {keepCoachAccess}; false = full hand-off, retires the coach link but keeps entitlement + re-key) and bulk invite (POST /coach/students/invite-bulk, per-student SAVEPOINT-isolated report) — backend #559/#560 + frontend #179 (co-access switch in the invite dialog + row-select "Invite selected to IG (N)" + result report). 2026-07-06 EDT — Prompt #1303 [dev is not available. what is the issue? — Tier B concurrency=0 took down dev auth/cors/ws; reverted all 36 Lambdas]
Bill: "dev is not available. what is the issue?"
Diagnosis: AWS dev profile itself works (sts:GetCallerIdentity returns willb77-dev in [aws-account]). "dev" = the dev *environment* — dev.inspiresgenius.com static site serves HTTP 200 (CloudFront cache), but every API call fails. Root cause: 2026-07-04 Tier B execute set ReservedConcurrentExecutions=0 on 36 Lambdas including on-demand infra: ig-dev-auth-service (login/token refresh), ig-dev-cors-options (CORS preflight for every browser call), ig-dev-ws-proxy (WebSocket), ig-dev-user-service, ig-dev-dashboard-service, etc. Phase 2's 30-day idle check + the executor's 24h safety re-check both saw them as idle because Bill hadn't touched dev; on next real request they throttle to 429 → effective total-outage.
Fix: ran delete-function-concurrency on all 36 Lambdas. 35 mgmt ([aws-account] via --profile dev) + 1 Development ([aws-account] via assume-role OrganizationAccountAccessRole). 36/36 succeeded. Rollback manifest updated (86 entries, 36 new B-revert rows).
Verified restored: GET https://[aws-host]/v1/auth/health → HTTP 200 (was throttled). get-function-concurrency returns empty body on all 6 spot-checked Lambdas — no reserved cap, uses account default (1000).
Follow-up task #76 opened: Phase 2 analyze_lambda() needs to detect API-GW/EventBridge/SNS/SQS/ELB trigger sources via list-event-source-mappings + resource-based policy inspection; on-demand infra Lambdas should be classified on-demand-infra and forced off Tier B regardless of invocation count. Invocation count tells you nobody's using the *product*, not whether the Lambda is infrastructure that would break the product if capped.
Lesson: "no invocations 30d" ≠ "safe to cap concurrency". A dormant call-tree can still be load-bearing.

2026-04-14 — Prompt #915 [MemoryManager Wiring]

All 24 received HTTP 200 with non-empty content (3.5–19.2s latency, avg 6.5s via Lambda Duration metric). Lenient pass rate 22/24; strict pass rate 17/24. Methodology delta: plan specifies https://dev.inspiresgenius.com/v1/agents/chat, but on dev that hostname serves the SPA — the actual API gateway is https://[aws-host]. The chat route's API GW integration nj5msbs targets the agent-engine ALB → ECS Fargate, but the ECS task hits asyncpg TimeoutError against Aurora's cluster endpoint (DB env points at the cluster, not the RDS Proxy), each request stacks 60–90s of retries, blowing the 30s API GW HTTP-API integration timeout (max allowed). Matrix completed via direct aws lambda invoke ig-dev-agent-engine (Mangum handler, RDS Proxy, 120s Lambda ceiling).
